# Iran and Ceasefire
* **Iran shuts down the Strait of Hormuz after hitting container ship:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy announced Saturday that the Strait would be "closed until further notice."
* According to the IRGC, the decision came after a vessel attempted to transit through an "unapproved route" after disabling its tracking systems and ignoring orders to change course. It said it struck the vessel "with warning fire," forcing it to stop.
* Oman [rescued](https://substack.com/redirect/259a27fa-ea81-4113-ab7e-799f13af41a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 23 crew members from the Cyprus-flagged container ship M/V GFS Galaxy after the container ship caught fire overnight near the Musandam Peninsula, according to the UKMTO monitoring organization. One sailor remains missing. A U.S. official later confirmed to Axios that the GFS Galaxy sustained heavy damage.
* The Iran-U.S. memorandum of understanding states that commercial vessel traffic would be fully restored within 30 days of the agreement, and that Iran "will make arrangements using its best efforts for the safe passage of commercial vessels." Tehran, therefore, insists that oversight and management of the Strait remains under its control, and that navigation be conducted through its northern route, rather than through the southern U.S.- and allied-backed corridor along the Omani coast. Iran has also maintained that decisions regarding the administration of the Strait will be made exclusively by Tehran and Oman, in dialogue with other Persian Gulf states, in accordance with the MOU.
* The Iranian navy warned that it would "respond severely" to any further violations, noting that it would also "target enemy bases" in the region.
* Two other vessels were fired at on Monday, with the IRGC saying it fired warning shots at two ships attempting to "illegally" cross the Strait.
* **U.S. launches third wave of strikes on Iran:** U.S. Central Command [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/9afae5fe-7d60-451e-9e5d-849d899a2d17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Saturday evening that it had begun a third round of strikes on the country.
* Explosions were heard in the southern coastal cities of Bandar Abbas, Bandar Jask, Sirik, Asaluyeh, and Bushehr in the Bushehr province, and the nearby cities of Kangan, Dayyer, and Chabahar. Explosions were also heard in Erbil in Iranian Kurdistan, near the Iraqi border.
* A statement from CENTCOM following Saturday's strikes [said](https://substack.com/redirect/6baaba37-c2d1-4dc6-9378-de9930dcdfd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the U.S. had struck 140 "military targets," including "missile and drone sites, naval assets, ammunition depots, communications networks, and coastal surveillance positions."
* The U.S. [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/7d5dd9f0-8002-45bb-ad1c-93f6e4cf0f3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) another round of strikes on Sunday, per CENTCOM, with Iranian media reporting strikes and explosions heard in Bandar Abbas, Jask, Sirik, and Qeshm Island.
* A strike on Sunday [destroyed](https://substack.com/redirect/58b2f72d-4a24-4842-b470-12bdb5072d35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a hangar at Iran's Omidiyeh Airport, in the central Khuzestan province, according to footage purporting to be from the site circulating online.
* Iran's Foreign Ministry [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/571e0c98-41ad-4c38-b150-df01b4badb36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the U.S. strikes in a Sunday statement, calling them "savage attacks" that violate the UN Charter, and issued a warning to Gulf states that host U.S. bases, saying that that relationship makes them a "legitimate target of defensive strikes" by Iran's armed forces. It also chastised the UN for its "non-constructive approach" to U.S. violations of the organization's rules.
* **Iran retaliates, hitting U.S. Gulf bases:** Iran fired upon U.S. military sites in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, the UAE, and Oman.
* Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan, a U.S. drone command centre in Bahrain and other air bases, including Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, according to the Islamic Republic News Agency. The IRGC also claimed attacks on what it described as U.S. military facilities and infrastructure in Juffair, Bahrain, as well as a vessel-detection radar in Oman.
* Kuwait said some of its border posts were damaged, and Qatar and the UAE confirmed that they had intercepted Iranian missiles.
* Smoke was seen [rising](https://substack.com/redirect/022f0b57-9fa6-4836-aa2c-bd1e83d7b7f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters in Manama, Bahrain on Sunday morning, according to video footage shared online.
* The retaliatory attacks [continued](https://substack.com/redirect/cacc3957-69b9-4ac9-811d-7bcdeea5419c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday morning, with the militaries of Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait reporting strikes.
* **Trump claims Hormuz remains open:** President Donald Trump [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/6dfc8178-e697-4fe2-be46-5523abc6f552?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a Sunday appearance before NBC's Meet the Press that U.S. military action had kept the Strait of Hormuz open even as Tehran announced its closure and as hostilities between the U.S. and Iran continued.
* "It's open," Trump said, adding that the U.S. had "bombed the hell out of" Iran on Saturday evening.
* Trump framed the situation as a product of Iran's "giving up" on a deal, which he called a "perfect deal" for the U.S., and which he alleged, without substantiating, forbade them from pursuing any further nuclear development.
* **Drop Site 's Jeremy Scahill **[reported](https://substack.com/redirect/853906b2-4546-4bcc-9234-0e55d8ebf442?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the White House's "deliberate media disinformation campaign" regarding these negotiations on Saturday, with the U.S. using Axios to pin responsibility for a recent attack in the Strait on a "rogue sect" in the military and to say that Tehran was considering announcing new transit routes with Oman.
* The official told Scahill the campaign is "a very deliberate and coordinated media campaign designed to pressure us into changing our decision." "We had already clearly told the Qataris and Omanis about our firm and final decision: Iran will not allow anyone to disrupt our security and oversight management of the Strait of Hormuz," he added.
* **Trump announces reimposition of U.S. blockade; Iran 's armed forces warn against U.S. interference: **In a post on Truth Social,**** Donald Trump announced the reinstatement of a blockade on Iranian ports, under which Iranian ships and customers would be barred from entering or leaving while other countries retain access. In the post, Trump also declared the U.S. "the Guardian of the Hormuz Strait" while adding that Washington would seek reimbursement at a rate of 20% on all cargo shipped through the waterway to cover the costs of providing security.
* Following Trump's comments, Iran's unified armed forces command warned the U.S. against intervening in the Strait. Iranian forces would "deal severely with any disruption and insecurity" outside Tehran's designated shipping route, said Ebrahim Zolfaghari, spokesman for the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, warning that any logistical support for the U.S. military would be considered "a war against Iran's sovereignty and national security" that could "engulf all the countries in the region."
* **Iran repairing nuclear, missile sites hit in U.S.-Israeli strikes, CNN reports:** Iran has been [repairing](https://substack.com/redirect/0131dd95-2553-4a0e-af47-16b4babc48a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nuclear and missile sites damaged in U.S.-Israeli strikes, a CNN visual investigation published on Saturday purported to show.
* Satellite images show reconstruction at the Parchin complex, activity at the underground Pickaxe Mountain facility, and coverings over buildings at Natanz and Isfahan, which experts told CNN may conceal efforts to recover nuclear material from satellite observation and block IAEA inspectors.
* Separate imagery showed excavators and dump trucks clearing entrances to underground missile bases, with at least 50 of 69 tunnel access points examined reopened, potentially restoring access to missiles trapped by the strikes.
* Iran had pledged to "maintain the status quo" of its civilian nuclear program until a final deal could be reached between itself and the U.S. in the memorandum of understanding.
* **Oil market spikes:** Oil futures [jumped](https://substack.com/redirect/9cc25c2f-fe5d-423f-a39e-276cab32a78d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 3% as markets opened Sunday, amid renewed U.S.-Iran attacks and fears of further disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.
* Brent crude rose to roughly $78.71 a barrel, nearly 10% above its level before Donald Trump declared the MOU with Iran "over."

# Lebanon
* **Israeli ceasefire violations continue across south Lebanon with shelling, a drone attack, and home demolitions:** An Israeli drone [dropped](https://substack.com/redirect/5f39ccce-3629-4c2e-8352-de49d07c68f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an incendiary bomb on Al-Tahra hill in the town of Kfar Reman in the district of Nabatieh on Monday, while intermittent Israeli artillery shelling targeted the area between Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Kfartebnit, according to the state's National News Agency (NNA). In Marjayoun, the Israeli army [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/95900ff3-95d9-4c16-bd0b-7f5833bbd75b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and burned homes in the southern neighbourhoods of the border town of Hadatha.
* **Lebanon 's Aoun says he will urge Trump to pressure Israel ahead of White House visit: **Lebanese President Joseph Aoun [said](https://substack.com/redirect/07a3070f-5144-4e7e-8818-686b4409c487?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that only the Lebanese state and army are capable of protecting the country's citizens, stressing that he would not compromise on Lebanon's south or its rights. Speaking ahead of a planned July 21 meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House, Aoun said he would ask Trump to exert pressure on Israel to fully withdraw from Lebanese territory, commit to having no territorial ambitions in Lebanon, and implement the terms agreed under the "framework agreement" as well as Lebanon's demands.
* **Open letter from residents of southern Lebanon:** Amid ongoing Israeli violations in the south, a coalition representing residents of Lebanese border villages [called](https://substack.com/redirect/b9c93980-85a4-4596-a1ff-bba829002487?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for urgent action to stop the ongoing "destruction" of their communities. The group said more than 60 villages remain occupied and that Israel is changing their "geographic, topographic and demographic" character. It urged President Joseph Aoun to halt any negotiations until the "bulldozing, demolitions and burning" stop, Israeli forces withdraw, displaced residents are allowed to return, and reconstruction begins.
* **Israeli Defense Minister: Southern Lebanon subjected to Gaza-like destruction; 90% of homes destroyed:** Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz [said](https://substack.com/redirect/6933e68c-a419-4b10-b998-d7398f9f5258?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an interview Saturday that Israeli forces had demolished homes in 24 villages along Lebanon's southern border, saying the military had applied the "Rafah model" used in Gaza. "I said that Southern Lebanon would become Gaza... We would destroy everything there. And that is what we did," Katz said. He added that the army had "systematically flattened the villages with bulldozers and explosives," adding that 90% of homes had been destroyed, amounting to between 15,000 and 20,000 houses.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded:** Over the last 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed, one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and 32 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,231 killed, with 173,686 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,108 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,578, while 800 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israel kills two Palestinians in Gaza on Monday:** Two Palestinians were killed in separate Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Monday, according to WAFA. One person was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/696e0282-a942-4aaa-86e1-c13e9b46f5e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and several others injured after an Israeli airstrike targeted a motorcycle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City. Earlier, another Palestinian was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/e219a24c-3456-4e79-90d0-d1e8ee250d01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when an Israeli strike hit a home in the Al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza.
* **Israeli strikes on Gaza continue over the weekend:**
* Israeli forces [repeatedly](https://substack.com/redirect/50116dff-8c19-4f99-b59e-3c708ea0ba8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) struck a civilian vehicle near the Nuseirat camp in central Gaza on Saturday, killing one person and wounding several others, including children. The first strike, according to residents of the area, left everyone unscathed. Israeli forces then struck a person trying to flee the vehicle, killed another person who retreated to the shoreline, and launched a drone strike on civilians attempting to rescue the wounded.
* Another Israeli drone strike on Saturday killed a man in Khan Younis, with 11 others wounded.
* Israel killed eight Palestinians, including a child, on Sunday, and continued to shell and demolish houses across the Strip.
* An Israeli [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/aa644fbd-8122-4dda-bc44-b20a688ff090?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on tents in Khan Younis on Sunday killed one and wounded others, and a separate strike by an Israeli drone killed four others near Gaza City.
* Three Palestinians, including a young girl, died on Sunday from wounds they sustained during an Israeli attack on the Al-Bureij refugee camp,
* Palestinian photojournalist Saed Hasaballah was [wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/ea49c9e5-09ff-42bb-8e8c-2212c51f7b4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday while covering an Israeli strike in Gaza City after four air strikes hit a single-story home. Hasaballah said he suffered injuries to his left hand and back. "This is the second time... but it will not stop me from continuing to report the truth from the heart of the field...so Gaza's voice continues to reach the world," he said in a statement posted from the hospital.
* **Israeli forces kill Palestinian near separation wall north of occupied Jerusalem:** A 20-year-old Palestinian was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/7225b087-7e4e-46c8-993c-78cae68ce0f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Israeli forces on Monday morning near the separation wall in the town of Bir Nabala, northeast of occupied Jerusalem, WAFA reported. The killing comes amid repeated shootings near the separation wall, where Palestinians, many of them workers attempting to reach jobs in Jerusalem and the '48 territories inside of Israel, are frequently targeted by Israeli forces. At least 39 workers have been shot near the wall since the start of 2026, while two were killed in May, according to the Jerusalem Governorate.
* **Armed settlers block Rep. Ro Khanna in West Bank village:** Armed Israeli settlers [blocked](https://substack.com/redirect/e75b8008-36ae-48bc-81ee-a0a7657d6a92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, D-Calif., from leaving Khirbet Zanuta in the occupied West Bank for 90 minutes on Saturday as Israeli troops stood by and later blocked the road themselves, the New York Times reported, citing footage from the congressman and his team.
* Khanna, who was on a three-day, Palestinian-led tour meeting Palestinian families, local officials and business owners, told the Times the episode showed how difficult a two-state solution would be given the number of violent settlers who would need to be removed. "We really saw the apartheid-like conditions, the inequality," he said.
* Khanna [described](https://substack.com/redirect/fc342896-ab0b-4609-a215-5ae45c0ad98a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the encounter in additional detail to Reuters, noting that settlers had destroyed a school in the village and much of the village itself, and had menaced its residents afterwards. "These hoodlums come in with machine guns, an M4, an American-made machine gun, and they detain us," he said. "They block off the road. And then they call the IDF, and the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans."
* In a statement regarding the attack, Khanna [highlighted](https://substack.com/redirect/f4dec4ee-f83c-47a8-9823-ad7a70c55bb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the work of Drop Site's Maysa Mustafa and of journalist Jasper Nathaniel, "and the many other journalists telling stories directly from Palestinians about what they're experiencing." Maysa spoke with Khanna about his experience in the occupied West Bank; a video of their discussion is available [here](https://substack.com/redirect/2ff2a6f1-772e-48d9-bc36-21380cbb4fd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Separately on Saturday, U.S. Sen. Chris Van Hollen [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/a16274b2-a67f-47de-bfc7-3872185e3494?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of "simply lying" when he claimed there had been transparency around the killings of Americans in the occupied West Bank. Van Hollen noted that nine Americans, including Palestinian American Saif Musallet, have been killed by Israeli settlers or forces over the past four years, and that no Israeli had been held to serious account as a result.
* Netanyahu [responded](https://substack.com/redirect/aa495f8b-edab-42b4-ba93-44b6bf4295d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) directly to Khanna's detention in the West Bank, telling NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday that the settlers were "150 juvenile delinquents that are not part of that community," despite Khanna's assertions that they were coordinating with the country's military.
* **Israel advances plan for "largest settlement enclave" in East Jerusalem's Umm Lison: **Israeli authorities [approved](https://substack.com/redirect/73582bba-199b-436c-b259-3f95fbda891e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) plans to advance the construction of around 450 illegal settlement housing units inside the Palestinian neighbourhood of Umm Lison in occupied East Jerusalem, according to the Israeli rights group Ir Amim via Anadolu Agency. The organisation said the project, which had been frozen for more than two years, could bring around 2,000 Israeli settlers into the neighbourhood.
* The Jerusalem Governorate [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4e7bc479-82ae-4e3a-9217-4aee8c10e0b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the project would create the largest settlement enclave inside a Palestinian neighbourhood in occupied East Jerusalem and reflects "an integrated settler-colonial project," rather than isolated violations.
* **Gaza health ministry warns ambulance fleet nearing "complete paralysis": **Gaza's Health Ministry [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/3aedbc98-a0fa-4f8a-8c73-e6bc9ea4b441?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Saturday that the territory's medical transport system is nearing "complete paralysis" amid Israel's continued ban on the entry of tires and spare parts, saying 70% of its remaining ambulances and transport vehicles are out of service due to direct Israeli attacks, mechanical failures and shortage of parts.

# U.S. News
_By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at[ Julian@dropsitenews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/cd719727-7638-40d2-bf95-38cee5000b1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
* **Sen. Lindsey Graham dead at 71: Lindsey Graham, the Republican senator** who represented South Carolina in the Senate for 23 years, [passed away](https://substack.com/redirect/022f0b57-9fa6-4836-aa2c-bd1e83d7b7f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "from a sudden illness" on Saturday, a statement from his office confirmed. The Washington, D.C., chief medical examiner later attributed his death to "aortic dissection due to arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease."
* Graham, a onetime Trump critic turned close ally, was one of Congress' most outspoken hawks, calling as early as 2010 for a preemptive strike on Iran and making numerous belligerent (and at times, racist) statements about the country. Graham was a forceful advocate for the current war, with Politico reporting in March that Graham told Trump the war could be his "Berlin Wall" moment.
* Graham was also an avowed supporter of Israel, leading him to receive tributes from **Benjamin Netanyahu** (who told Meet the Press on Sunday that Graham had urged him to strike Iran as well) and from **Itamar Ben Gvir** , the far-right Israeli security minister, who said Graham's "unwavering support, courage, and moral clarity earned him the admiration of millions of Israelis."
* Politico [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/5634f229-44fd-4348-b2b1-1ebf809384d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Republican **Rep. Nancy Mace** is considering a bid for Graham's Senate seat. Mace, who is set to vacate her coastal House seat after finishing fifth in this year's gubernatorial primary, has clashed with Trump over the release of the **Jeffrey Epstein** files.
* **McConnell addresses health speculation: Sen. Mitch McConnell** , 84, [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/ce465955-c1ca-41b8-b913-65acd50a1fd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a statement and photo on Sunday in response to weeks of speculation about his health, saying a fall left him "briefly unconscious" and led to his hospitalization last month.
* McConnell said that, after his fall, he was treated for mild pneumonia and is now in a rehabilitation facility.
* In the statement, McConnell said that he was "regaining [his] strength," but gave no timeline for a Senate return.

* Alongside **Sen. Graham** 's death, his absence temporarily narrows the Republican majority in the Senate to 51-47.
* **Minnesota pulls its National Guard from D.C:** Minnesota **Gov. Tim Walz** [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/1c004faa-8938-4f1d-b456-89ed775a6083?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Saturday that he would be pulling the state's National Guard members from Washington, D.C. after they were seen patrolling neighborhoods far from the National Mall, despite orders to strictly assist in the city's 250th anniversary celebrations.
* Thousands of National Guard troops from nearly two dozen states have been in D.C. for months as Trump's federal task force has grown to more than 5,100 troops and costs upward of $3 million a day.
* **Sen. Gary Peters endorses Haley Stevens in Michigan Democratic primary** : Outgoing Michigan **Sen.** **Gary Peters** [endorsed](https://substack.com/redirect/5b41505b-afa0-4af4-8e87-f8703d6d9b9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Rep. Haley Stevens** as his successor on Monday, reversing his earlier stance of neutrality and joining a growing push by Democratic leaders and pro-Israel groups to help her defeat progressive rival **Abdul El-Sayed** ahead of the August 4 primary.
* Peters, retiring after 12 years in the Senate, said Stevens "will be ready on day one to fight for Michigan." Senate Democratic leader **Chuck Schumer** and Sens. **Ruben Gallego** and **Catherine Cortez Masto** have also endorsed Stevens.
* El-Sayed has received endorsements from Sens. **Bernie Sanders** and **Chris Van Hollen**.
* **Attacks on progressive Michigan congressional candidate from Democratic establishment:** A Saturday report from HuffPost [highlighted](https://substack.com/redirect/ff229345-6bfa-4f20-bb69-d800d355820c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a quote from a 2024 podcast in which progressive congressional candidate and Sunrise Movement cofounder **William Lawrence** said that "the older generation" of Black Democratic Party leaders "defangs the white left" in its attempts to resist "capitalist, imperialist American power." He pointed to younger Black voters moving away from Democrats and asked his guest, a co-founder of Black 4 Palestine, whether a younger Black left could break that dynamic and help build a different political alignment.
* Lawrence apologized for the comments, which he called "clumsy," but added that "national elected leaders across race, ethnicity, age and gender have been supporters of unnecessary U.S. wars. This poses a challenge to the anti-war movement."
* The article's framing follows similar attacks by mainstream Democratic organizations like EMILY's List, Center for American Progress CEO **Neera Tanden** , and the Congressional Black Caucus Political Action Committee.
* Lawrence has been endorsed by Sen. **Bernie Sanders** and by Michigan congresswoman**Rashida Tlaib**.
* **UAW 's Shawn Fain says his Gaza advocacy prompted DOJ probe: **The Justice Department has [opened](https://substack.com/redirect/fbc66d8b-aa9c-46e4-8f20-9ac93ccf0c97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a grand jury investigation into allegations that UAW President Shawn Fain improperly used his authority to benefit his fiancee and retaliated against union official Rich Boyer, both Reuters and the New York Times reported on Sunday.
* Fain, who is seeking re-election to his position, denied the claims Sunday and said Boyer fed the union's federal monitor "false allegations." He accused monitor Neil Barofsky of holding a political grudge because the UAW backed a ceasefire in Gaza, citing a heated 2024 dispute over the union's anti-war position.
* Fain noted that he has hired lawyers and said he is considering all legal options.
* **Trump is seeking to extradite pro-Palestine funder from Spain** : **Fergie Cox Chambers** was arrested on Friday in Ibiza and faces an extradition hearing Thursday.
* Chambers is an heir to the Cox Enterprises family fortune. According to a press release, he received $250 million after cutting ties with his family and has donated over £1 million to humanitarian projects in Gaza.
* According to[ The Grayzone](https://substack.com/redirect/a3a0a4ac-d942-4f24-bfd8-6959ad0d5242?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which obtained his sealed indictment, the U.S. is pursuing charges of terrorism financing. "The sealed indictment offers no evidence that Chambers has donated any money to 'foreign terrorist organizations,'" The Grayzone reports. "It merely states 'Chambers made numerous transfers of funds from banks in the US to banks in Tunisia,' where he relocated in late 2023."

# Other International News
* **Former Qatari Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani dies at 74:** Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the former emir who elevated Qatar from a little-known emirate into a wealthy and globally influential state, [died](https://substack.com/redirect/4c967cc1-9cd1-45aa-ad00-123618dd8098?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sunday at age 74, the Qatari royal court announced. The court did not specify a cause of death.
* Sheikh Hamad seized power from his father, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad, in a 1995 coup and ruled for 28 years before voluntarily handing power to his son, current emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in 2013.
* In the course of his reign, Hamad oversaw a 24-fold expansion of Qatar's economy through its natural gas industry, founded Al Jazeera, built a sovereign wealth fund now managing roughly $600 billion, and won hosting rights for the 2022 World Cup.
* During a landmark 2012 visit to Gaza, and as the only Arab leader to visit the Strip during Israel's blockade, Hamad announced more than $400 million for housing, infrastructure, and reconstruction projects, including Hamad City in Khan Younis and the Sheikh Hamad Rehabilitation and Prosthetics Hospital. Many of those projects were later destroyed or heavily damaged during Israel's war on Gaza. Palestinians widely credited him with breaking Gaza's political isolation and providing sustained support for the enclave.
* **Russian, Ukrainian attacks kill nine:** Russian drones and missiles [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/0e72cab8-6f89-401f-9bbe-32291ee1c3e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four people in Ukraine overnight into Sunday, including three in the central Dnipropetrovsk region and one in Kherson, while Ukrainian strikes killed five people in Russia and Russian-occupied Ukraine, including four in the occupied town of Enerhodar and one in Russia's Samara region, Al Jazeera reported.
* At least 25 heads of state from the "Coalition of the Willing" are slated to meet in Paris on Monday to discuss further support for Ukraine and how to end the war.
* **Norway pushes for Israel 's suspension from FIFA, Politico reports: **Norway is [using](https://substack.com/redirect/00e32b09-4243-44b4-8e44-7fb8249c06b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its influence inside soccer to push for Israel's suspension from FIFA, Politico reported on Saturday.
* Lise Klaveness, the Norwegian Football Federation's President, is reportedly leading the campaign for the suspension, arguing that FIFA's ban on Russia after its invasion of Ukraine represents a double standard as Israel continues its assault on Gaza.
* The campaign was first launched by the Palestinian Football Association in 2024 over Israel's actions in Gaza, its discrimination against Arab athletes, and its inclusion of clubs based in the occupied West Bank.
* **Malian army retakes Anefis from rebels, loses about 30 troops:** The Malian army [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/a6bdc748-8f4a-41e6-868d-357af48405e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday that around 30 soldiers were killed and about 60 wounded, some seriously, during an operation that retook the northern town of Anefis from Tuareg separatists and fighters linked to al-Qaeda who had captured it in coordinated attacks on July 4.
* The Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front said a day earlier that it had lost some of its best fighters in the battle but had inflicted the heaviest losses in its history in the region.
* The clashes come amid an escalating insurgency against the government and its allied Russian mercenary groups by separatists and fighters tied to al-Qaeda.
* **Syria 's new transitional parliament holds first session: **Syria's transitional parliament, the newly formed 210-seat People's Assembly, [convened](https://substack.com/redirect/63d16b38-5fca-4c63-86ad-1493601f97b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its inaugural session in Damascus on Sunday, with members taking the constitutional oath more than 18 months after longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad was toppled by rebels led by current president, Ahmed al-Sharaa.
* Two-thirds of representatives were chosen by regional electoral colleges held last year, with officials arguing that nationwide elections were not yet feasible due to the logistical challenges created by the country's decades-long civil war. Al-Sharaa appointed the remaining 70 this month.
* The body's main task will be drafting a new constitution, and al-Sharaa emphasized its priorities would include strengthening the economy, bolstering public services, and attracting foreign investment into the country.
* **South Korean court sentences former President Yoon Suk-yeol to two years:** A Seoul Central District Court [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/47f5ed7f-5151-4cd3-a0f7-cfd3e059c6b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol, 65, to two years in prison on Monday, after finding him guilty of illegally receiving free opinion polling services worth 270 million won ($179,800) from a political broker, Reuters reported.
* The court ruling adds to the eight legal cases Yoon faces, including an appeal of a life sentence for masterminding an insurrection tied to his 2024 martial law declaration and a Supreme Court ruling last week finalizing a separate seven-year sentence for obstructing authorities' attempts to arrest him.
* **EU pledges €120 million for Moldova's air defenses:** The European Union [approved](https://substack.com/redirect/e7d59581-cfda-4bae-8f42-d6d0e78be37b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) €120 million in aid through the European Peace Facility to strengthen Moldova's air defense capabilities following alleged incursions by Russian drones into its airspace. The increased funding--which exceeded prior estimates for EU support--follows repeated concerns about spillover from the war in neighboring Ukraine, including a report last November that Russian drones had entered Moldovan airspace.

Iran and Ceasefire Iran shuts down the Strait of Hormuz after hitting container ship: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy announced Saturday that the Strait would be "closed until further notice." According to the IRGC, the decision came after a vessel attempted to transit through an "unapproved route" after disabling its tracking systems and ignoring orders to change course. It said it struck the vessel "with warning fire," forcing it to stop. Oman 23 crew members from the Cyprus-flagged container ship M/V GFS Galaxy after the container ship caught fire overnight near the Musandam Peninsula, according to the UKMTO monitoring organization. One sailor remains missing. A U.S. official later confirmed to Axios that the GFS Galaxy sustained heavy damage. The Iran-U.S. memorandum of understanding states that commercial vessel traffic would be fully restored within 30 days of the agreement, and that Iran "will make arrangements using its best efforts for the safe passage of commercial vessels." Tehran, therefore, insists that oversight and management of the Strait remains under its control, and that navigation be conducted through its northern route, rather than through the southern U.S.- and allied-backed corridor along the Omani coast. Iran has also maintained that decisions regarding the administration of the Strait will be made exclusively by Tehran and Oman, in dialogue with other Persian Gulf states, in accordance with the MOU. The Iranian navy warned that it would "respond severely" to any further violations, noting that it would also "target enemy bases" in the region. Two other vessels were fired at on Monday, with the IRGC saying it fired warning shots at two ships attempting to "illegally" cross the Strait. U.S. launches third wave of strikes on Iran: U.S. Central Command on Saturday evening that it had begun a third round of strikes on the country. Explosions were heard in the southern coastal cities of Bandar Abbas, Bandar Jask, Sirik, Asaluyeh, and Bushehr in the Bushehr province, and the nearby cities of Kangan, Dayyer, and Chabahar. Explosions were also heard in Erbil in Iranian Kurdistan, near the Iraqi border. A statement from CENTCOM following Saturday's strikes that the U.S. had struck 140 "military targets," including "missile and drone sites, naval assets, ammunition depots, communications networks, and coastal surveillance positions." The U.S. another round of strikes on Sunday, per CENTCOM, with Iranian media reporting strikes and explosions heard in Bandar Abbas, Jask, Sirik, and Qeshm Island. A strike on Sunday a hangar at Iran's Omidiyeh Airport, in the central Khuzestan province, according to footage purporting to be from the site circulating online. Iran's Foreign Ministry the U.S. strikes in a Sunday statement, calling them "savage attacks" that violate the UN Charter, and issued a warning to Gulf states that host U.S. bases, saying that that relationship makes them a "legitimate target of defensive strikes" by Iran's armed forces. It also chastised the UN for its "non-constructive approach" to U.S. violations of the organization's rules. Iran retaliates, hitting U.S. Gulf bases: Iran fired upon U.S. military sites in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, the UAE, and Oman. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan, a U.S. drone command centre in Bahrain and other air bases, including Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, according to the Islamic Republic News Agency. The IRGC also claimed attacks on what it described as U.S. military facilities and infrastructure in Juffair, Bahrain, as well as a vessel-detection radar in Oman. Kuwait said some of its border posts were damaged, and Qatar and the UAE confirmed that they had intercepted Iranian missiles. Smoke was seen from the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters in Manama, Bahrain on Sunday morning, according to video footage shared online. The retaliatory attacks Monday morning, with the militaries of Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait reporting strikes. Trump claims Hormuz remains open: President Donald Trump in a Sunday appearance before NBC's Meet the Press that U.S. military action had kept the Strait of Hormuz open even as Tehran announced its closure and as hostilities between the U.S. and Iran continued. "It's open," Trump said, adding that the U.S. had "bombed the hell out of" Iran on Saturday evening. Trump framed the situation as a product of Iran's "giving up" on a deal, which he called a "perfect deal" for the U.S., and which he alleged, without substantiating, forbade them from pursuing any further nuclear development. Drop Site 's Jeremy Scahill on the White House's "deliberate media disinformation campaign" regarding these negotiations on Saturday, with the U.S. using Axios to pin responsibility for a recent attack in the Strait on a "rogue sect" in the military and to say that Tehran was considering announcing new transit routes with Oman. The official told Scahill the campaign is "a very deliberate and coordinated media campaign designed to pressure us into changing our decision." "We had already clearly told the Qataris and Omanis about our firm and final decision: Iran will not allow anyone to disrupt our security and oversight management of the Strait of Hormuz," he added. Trump announces reimposition of U.S. blockade; Iran 's armed forces warn against U.S. interference: In a post on Truth Social,** Donald Trump announced the reinstatement of a blockade on Iranian ports, under which Iranian ships and customers would be barred from entering or leaving while other countries retain access. In the post, Trump also declared the U.S. "the Guardian of the Hormuz Strait" while adding that Washington would seek reimbursement at a rate of 20% on all cargo shipped through the waterway to cover the costs of providing security. Following Trump's comments, Iran's unified armed forces command warned the U.S. against intervening in the Strait. Iranian forces would "deal severely with any disruption and insecurity" outside Tehran's designated shipping route, said Ebrahim Zolfaghari, spokesman for the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, warning that any logistical support for the U.S. military would be considered "a war against Iran's sovereignty and national security" that could "engulf all the countries in the region." Iran repairing nuclear, missile sites hit in U.S.-Israeli strikes, CNN reports: Iran has been nuclear and missile sites damaged in U.S.-Israeli strikes, a CNN visual investigation published on Saturday purported to show. Satellite images show reconstruction at the Parchin complex, activity at the underground Pickaxe Mountain facility, and coverings over buildings at Natanz and Isfahan, which experts told CNN may conceal efforts to recover nuclear material from satellite observation and block IAEA inspectors. Separate imagery showed excavators and dump trucks clearing entrances to underground missile bases, with at least 50 of 69 tunnel access points examined reopened, potentially restoring access to missiles trapped by the strikes. Iran had pledged to "maintain the status quo" of its civilian nuclear program until a final deal could be reached between itself and the U.S. in the memorandum of understanding. Oil market spikes: Oil futures more than 3% as markets opened Sunday, amid renewed U.S.-Iran attacks and fears of further disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude rose to roughly $78.71 a barrel, nearly 10% above its level before Donald Trump declared the MOU with Iran "over." Lebanon Israeli ceasefire violations continue across south Lebanon with shelling, a drone attack, and home demolitions: An Israeli drone an incendiary bomb on Al-Tahra hill in the town of Kfar Reman in the district of Nabatieh on Monday, while intermittent Israeli artillery shelling targeted the area between Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Kfartebnit, according to the state's National News Agency (NNA). In Marjayoun, the Israeli army and burned homes in the southern neighbourhoods of the border town of Hadatha. Lebanon 's Aoun says he will urge Trump to pressure Israel ahead of White House visit: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun on Monday that only the Lebanese state and army are capable of protecting the country's citizens, stressing that he would not compromise on Lebanon's south or its rights. Speaking ahead of a planned July 21 meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House, Aoun said he would ask Trump to exert pressure on Israel to fully withdraw from Lebanese territory, commit to having no territorial ambitions in Lebanon, and implement the terms agreed under the "framework agreement" as well as Lebanon's demands. Open letter from residents of southern Lebanon: Amid ongoing Israeli violations in the south, a coalition representing residents of Lebanese border villages for urgent action to stop the ongoing "destruction" of their communities. The group said more than 60 villages remain occupied and that Israel is changing their "geographic, topographic and demographic" character. It urged President Joseph Aoun to halt any negotiations until the "bulldozing, demolitions and burning" stop, Israeli forces withdraw, displaced residents are allowed to return, and reconstruction begins. Israeli Defense Minister: Southern Lebanon subjected to Gaza-like destruction; 90% of homes destroyed: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz in an interview Saturday that Israeli forces had demolished homes in 24 villages along Lebanon's southern border, saying the military had applied the "Rafah model" used in Gaza. "I said that Southern Lebanon would become Gaza... We would destroy everything there. And that is what we did," Katz said. He added that the army had "systematically flattened the villages with bulldozers and explosives," adding that 90% of homes had been destroyed, amounting to between 15,000 and 20,000 houses. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed, one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and 32 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,231 killed, with 173,686 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,108 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,578, while 800 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel kills two Palestinians in Gaza on Monday: Two Palestinians were killed in separate Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Monday, according to WAFA. One person was and several others injured after an Israeli airstrike targeted a motorcycle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City. Earlier, another Palestinian was when an Israeli strike hit a home in the Al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza. Israeli strikes on Gaza continue over the weekend: Israeli forces struck a civilian vehicle near the Nuseirat camp in central Gaza on Saturday, killing one person and wounding several others, including children. The first strike, according to residents of the area, left everyone unscathed. Israeli forces then struck a person trying to flee the vehicle, killed another person who retreated to the shoreline, and launched a drone strike on civilians attempting to rescue the wounded. Another Israeli drone strike on Saturday killed a man in Khan Younis, with 11 others wounded. Israel killed eight Palestinians, including a child, on Sunday, and continued to shell and demolish houses across the Strip. An Israeli on tents in Khan Younis on Sunday killed one and wounded others, and a separate strike by an Israeli drone killed four others near Gaza City. Three Palestinians, including a young girl, died on Sunday from wounds they sustained during an Israeli attack on the Al-Bureij refugee camp, Palestinian photojournalist Saed Hasaballah was on Sunday while covering an Israeli strike in Gaza City after four air strikes hit a single-story home. Hasaballah said he suffered injuries to his left hand and back. "This is the second time... but it will not stop me from continuing to report the truth from the heart of the field...so Gaza's voice continues to reach the world," he said in a statement posted from the hospital. Israeli forces kill Palestinian near separation wall north of occupied Jerusalem: A 20-year-old Palestinian was by Israeli forces on Monday morning near the separation wall in the town of Bir Nabala, northeast of occupied Jerusalem, WAFA reported. The killing comes amid repeated shootings near the separation wall, where Palestinians, many of them workers attempting to reach jobs in Jerusalem and the '48 territories inside of Israel, are frequently targeted by Israeli forces. At least 39 workers have been shot near the wall since the start of 2026, while two were killed in May, according to the Jerusalem Governorate. Armed settlers block Rep. Ro Khanna in West Bank village: Armed Israeli settlers U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, D-Calif., from leaving Khirbet Zanuta in the occupied West Bank for 90 minutes on Saturday as Israeli troops stood by and later blocked the road themselves, the New York Times reported, citing footage from the congressman and his team. Khanna, who was on a three-day, Palestinian-led tour meeting Palestinian families, local officials and business owners, told the Times the episode showed how difficult a two-state solution would be given the number of violent settlers who would need to be removed. "We really saw the apartheid-like conditions, the inequality," he said. Khanna the encounter in additional detail to Reuters, noting that settlers had destroyed a school in the village and much of the village itself, and had menaced its residents afterwards. "These hoodlums come in with machine guns, an M4, an American-made machine gun, and they detain us," he said. "They block off the road. And then they call the IDF, and the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans." In a statement regarding the attack, Khanna the work of Drop Site's Maysa Mustafa and of journalist Jasper Nathaniel, "and the many other journalists telling stories directly from Palestinians about what they're experiencing." Maysa spoke with Khanna about his experience in the occupied West Bank; a video of their discussion is available . Separately on Saturday, U.S. Sen. Chris Van Hollen Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of "simply lying" when he claimed there had been transparency around the killings of Americans in the occupied West Bank. Van Hollen noted that nine Americans, including Palestinian American Saif Musallet, have been killed by Israeli settlers or forces over the past four years, and that no Israeli had been held to serious account as a result. Netanyahu directly to Khanna's detention in the West Bank, telling NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday that the settlers were "150 juvenile delinquents that are not part of that community," despite Khanna's assertions that they were coordinating with the country's military. Israel advances plan for "largest settlement enclave" in East Jerusalem's Umm Lison: Israeli authorities plans to advance the construction of around 450 illegal settlement housing units inside the Palestinian neighbourhood of Umm Lison in occupied East Jerusalem, according to the Israeli rights group Ir Amim via Anadolu Agency. The organisation said the project, which had been frozen for more than two years, could bring around 2,000 Israeli settlers into the neighbourhood. The Jerusalem Governorate the project would create the largest settlement enclave inside a Palestinian neighbourhood in occupied East Jerusalem and reflects "an integrated settler-colonial project," rather than isolated violations. Gaza health ministry warns ambulance fleet nearing "complete paralysis": Gaza's Health Ministry on Saturday that the territory's medical transport system is nearing "complete paralysis" amid Israel's continued ban on the entry of tires and spare parts, saying 70% of its remaining ambulances and transport vehicles are out of service due to direct Israeli attacks, mechanical failures and shortage of parts. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Sen. Lindsey Graham dead at 71: Lindsey Graham, the Republican senator who represented South Carolina in the Senate for 23 years, "from a sudden illness" on Saturday, a statement from his office confirmed. The Washington, D.C., chief medical examiner later attributed his death to "aortic dissection due to arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease." Graham, a onetime Trump critic turned close ally, was one of Congress' most outspoken hawks, calling as early as 2010 for a preemptive strike on Iran and making numerous belligerent (and at times, racist) statements about the country. Graham was a forceful advocate for the current war, with Politico reporting in March that Graham told Trump the war could be his "Berlin Wall" moment. Graham was also an avowed supporter of Israel, leading him to receive tributes from Benjamin Netanyahu (who told Meet the Press on Sunday that Graham had urged him to strike Iran as well) and from Itamar Ben Gvir , the far-right Israeli security minister, who said Graham's "unwavering support, courage, and moral clarity earned him the admiration of millions of Israelis." Politico that Republican Rep. Nancy Mace is considering a bid for Graham's Senate seat. Mace, who is set to vacate her coastal House seat after finishing fifth in this year's gubernatorial primary, has clashed with Trump over the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files. McConnell addresses health speculation: Sen. Mitch McConnell , 84, a statement and photo on Sunday in response to weeks of speculation about his health, saying a fall left him "briefly unconscious" and led to his hospitalization last month. McConnell said that, after his fall, he was treated for mild pneumonia and is now in a rehabilitation facility. In the statement, McConnell said that he was "regaining [his] strength," but gave no timeline for a Senate return. Alongside Sen. Graham 's death, his absence temporarily narrows the Republican majority in the Senate to 51-47. Minnesota pulls its National Guard from D.C: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz on Saturday that he would be pulling the state's National Guard members from Washington, D.C. after they were seen patrolling neighborhoods far from the National Mall, despite orders to strictly assist in the city's 250th anniversary celebrations. Thousands of National Guard troops from nearly two dozen states have been in D.C. for months as Trump's federal task force has grown to more than 5,100 troops and costs upward of $3 million a day. Sen. Gary Peters endorses Haley Stevens in Michigan Democratic primary : Outgoing Michigan Sen. Gary Peters Rep. Haley Stevens as his successor on Monday, reversing his earlier stance of neutrality and joining a growing push by Democratic leaders and pro-Israel groups to help her defeat progressive rival Abdul El-Sayed ahead of the August 4 primary. Peters, retiring after 12 years in the Senate, said Stevens "will be ready on day one to fight for Michigan." Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and Sens. Ruben Gallego and Catherine Cortez Masto have also endorsed Stevens. El-Sayed has received endorsements from Sens. Bernie Sanders and Chris Van Hollen. Attacks on progressive Michigan congressional candidate from Democratic establishment: A Saturday report from HuffPost a quote from a 2024 podcast in which progressive congressional candidate and Sunrise Movement cofounder William Lawrence said that "the older generation" of Black Democratic Party leaders "defangs the white left" in its attempts to resist "capitalist, imperialist American power." He pointed to younger Black voters moving away from Democrats and asked his guest, a co-founder of Black 4 Palestine, whether a younger Black left could break that dynamic and help build a different political alignment. Lawrence apologized for the comments, which he called "clumsy," but added that "national elected leaders across race, ethnicity, age and gender have been supporters of unnecessary U.S. wars. This poses a challenge to the anti-war movement." The article's framing follows similar attacks by mainstream Democratic organizations like EMILY's List, Center for American Progress CEO Neera Tanden , and the Congressional Black Caucus Political Action Committee. Lawrence has been endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders and by Michigan congresswomanRashida Tlaib. UAW 's Shawn Fain says his Gaza advocacy prompted DOJ probe: The Justice Department has a grand jury investigation into allegations that UAW President Shawn Fain improperly used his authority to benefit his fiancee and retaliated against union official Rich Boyer, both Reuters and the New York Times reported on Sunday. Fain, who is seeking re-election to his position, denied the claims Sunday and said Boyer fed the union's federal monitor "false allegations." He accused monitor Neil Barofsky of holding a political grudge because the UAW backed a ceasefire in Gaza, citing a heated 2024 dispute over the union's anti-war position. Fain noted that he has hired lawyers and said he is considering all legal options. Trump is seeking to extradite pro-Palestine funder from Spain : Fergie Cox Chambers was arrested on Friday in Ibiza and faces an extradition hearing Thursday. Chambers is an heir to the Cox Enterprises family fortune. According to a press release, he received $250 million after cutting ties with his family and has donated over £1 million to humanitarian projects in Gaza. According to, which obtained his sealed indictment, the U.S. is pursuing charges of terrorism financing. "The sealed indictment offers no evidence that Chambers has donated any money to 'foreign terrorist organizations,'" The Grayzone reports. "It merely states 'Chambers made numerous transfers of funds from banks in the US to banks in Tunisia,' where he relocated in late 2023." Other International News Former Qatari Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani dies at 74: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the former emir who elevated Qatar from a little-known emirate into a wealthy and globally influential state, Sunday at age 74, the Qatari royal court announced. The court did not specify a cause of death. Sheikh Hamad seized power from his father, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad, in a 1995 coup and ruled for 28 years before voluntarily handing power to his son, current emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in 2013. In the course of his reign, Hamad oversaw a 24-fold expansion of Qatar's economy through its natural gas industry, founded Al Jazeera, built a sovereign wealth fund now managing roughly $600 billion, and won hosting rights for the 2022 World Cup. During a landmark 2012 visit to Gaza, and as the only Arab leader to visit the Strip during Israel's blockade, Hamad announced more than $400 million for housing, infrastructure, and reconstruction projects, including Hamad City in Khan Younis and the Sheikh Hamad Rehabilitation and Prosthetics Hospital. Many of those projects were later destroyed or heavily damaged during Israel's war on Gaza. Palestinians widely credited him with breaking Gaza's political isolation and providing sustained support for the enclave. Russian, Ukrainian attacks kill nine: Russian drones and missiles four people in Ukraine overnight into Sunday, including three in the central Dnipropetrovsk region and one in Kherson, while Ukrainian strikes killed five people in Russia and Russian-occupied Ukraine, including four in the occupied town of Enerhodar and one in Russia's Samara region, Al Jazeera reported. At least 25 heads of state from the "Coalition of the Willing" are slated to meet in Paris on Monday to discuss further support for Ukraine and how to end the war. Norway pushes for Israel 's suspension from FIFA, Politico reports: Norway is its influence inside soccer to push for Israel's suspension from FIFA, Politico reported on Saturday. Lise Klaveness, the Norwegian Football Federation's President, is reportedly leading the campaign for the suspension, arguing that FIFA's ban on Russia after its invasion of Ukraine represents a double standard as Israel continues its assault on Gaza. The campaign was first launched by the Palestinian Football Association in 2024 over Israel's actions in Gaza, its discrimination against Arab athletes, and its inclusion of clubs based in the occupied West Bank. Malian army retakes Anefis from rebels, loses about 30 troops: The Malian army on Sunday that around 30 soldiers were killed and about 60 wounded, some seriously, during an operation that retook the northern town of Anefis from Tuareg separatists and fighters linked to al-Qaeda who had captured it in coordinated attacks on July 4. The Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front said a day earlier that it had lost some of its best fighters in the battle but had inflicted the heaviest losses in its history in the region. The clashes come amid an escalating insurgency against the government and its allied Russian mercenary groups by separatists and fighters tied to al-Qaeda. Syria 's new transitional parliament holds first session: Syria's transitional parliament, the newly formed 210-seat People's Assembly, its inaugural session in Damascus on Sunday, with members taking the constitutional oath more than 18 months after longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad was toppled by rebels led by current president, Ahmed al-Sharaa. Two-thirds of representatives were chosen by regional electoral colleges held last year, with officials arguing that nationwide elections were not yet feasible due to the logistical challenges created by the country's decades-long civil war. Al-Sharaa appointed the remaining 70 this month. The body's main task will be drafting a new constitution, and al-Sharaa emphasized its priorities would include strengthening the economy, bolstering public services, and attracting foreign investment into the country. South Korean court sentences former President Yoon Suk-yeol to two years: A Seoul Central District Court former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol, 65, to two years in prison on Monday, after finding him guilty of illegally receiving free opinion polling services worth 270 million won ($179,800) from a political broker, Reuters reported. The court ruling adds to the eight legal cases Yoon faces, including an appeal of a life sentence for masterminding an insurrection tied to his 2024 martial law declaration and a Supreme Court ruling last week finalizing a separate seven-year sentence for obstructing authorities' attempts to arrest him. EU pledges €120 million for Moldova's air defenses: The European Union €120 million in aid through the European Peace Facility to strengthen Moldova's air defense capabilities following alleged incursions by Russian drones into its airspace. The increased funding--which exceeded prior estimates for EU support--follows repeated concerns about spillover from the war in neighboring Ukraine, including a report last November that Russian drones had entered Moldovan airspace. clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: A healthy workforce is a strong workforce
body:
Rising healthcare costs are hurting businesses across our state.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Across Texas, business owners are being forced to make difficult financial decisions as the cost of providing health insurance continues to rise.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260713_1_cost.6Fs_ti&refcode=em20260713-1553&amount=5&t=1&akid=1553%2E299639%2EjlXMiq)
Many are paying _higher_ premiums year after year. While others are being forced to pass those costs on to their employees through higher deductibles and out-of-pocket expenses.
No business owner should have to choose between providing quality healthcare for their employees and maintaining their business. Yet, that’s the impossible position too many Texas employers find themselves in today.
To put it plainly, for some businesses, rising healthcare costs mean less money available to hire new workers, increase wages, or invest back into their communities.
**This healthcare problem has evolved into an economic problem, Peter.**
When businesses struggle to afford health coverage, **_working families feel it too._**
While healthcare costs continue to climb, Greg Abbott has offered little relief for these businesses. The result? **Texas has one of the highest uninsured rates in the country.**
As governor, I'll work to lower healthcare costs, expand access to affordable coverage, and make it easier — not harder — for Texas businesses to provide quality health insurance to their employees. Because when our small businesses succeed, our workers succeed, and our economy grows stronger.
Texas businesses deserve a governor who understands that a **healthy workforce is a strong workforce.**

name: James Carville
subject: Democrats have needed this for a long time.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Folks, it’s James Carville.
I’ve spent nearly half a century helping Democrats win elections, and I’m gonna tell you something plainly:
For too long, we have waited until the house was already on fire before deciding to buy a hose.
We wait until a race becomes a crisis.
We wait until a great candidate is getting buried in attack ads.
We wait until Republicans have already built the infrastructure, raised the money, and defined the battlefield.
Then everybody starts running around asking what happened.
Well, Raja Krishnamoorthi has gone and done something about it.
He founded Equal Opportunity Now to find and support bold leaders and important causes before it’s too late — leaders who will stand up to Donald Trump and the MAGA movement, fight for working families, and actually deliver results.
And all I can say is:
FINALLY.
Finally, an organization that understands we cannot defeat MAGA with timid candidates, stale talking points, and a last-minute panic.
But Raja cannot build this by himself.
Will you contribute $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Equal Opportunity Now find, fund, and support the leaders Democrats need to start winning again? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
SUPPORT EQUAL OPPORTUNITY NOW! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Now, I know Raja.
He is smart. He is tough. And he knows firsthand what opportunity can mean.
His family came to this country with very little. They relied on public housing and food stamps. He worked his way from Peoria all the way to Congress.
And instead of pulling the ladder up behind him, Raja has spent his career fighting to make sure the next family gets the same shot.
That means standing up for workers.
Holding powerful corporations and corrupt politicians accountable.
Defending immigrants, voting rights, and every American targeted by Trump’s politics of division.
And now he is putting that experience toward building the next generation of Democratic leadership.
Here’s the truth: The leaders we need are already out there.
They are running for city council, state legislature, Congress, and offices most national donors are not paying attention to yet.
They have the courage.
They have the ideas.
What they do not always have is the money, infrastructure, and early support necessary to compete.
That is where Equal Opportunity Now comes in.
Please chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Raja build the organization Democrats should have built years ago. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
HELP DEMOCRATS WIN: DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
We’ve got a good battle plan, now, let’s help Raja build this damn thing.
-- James Carville
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

Equal Opportunity Now is d/b/a Reviving American Jobs Again PAC (RAJA PAC)

P.O. Box 68412,
Schaumburg, IL 60168
United States

name: Dylan for Wisconsin
subject: Investing in the Next Generation of Wisconsin Leaders
body:
I couldn't have done any of this without the people who believed in me. I'm asking Wisconsin to believe in a new generation of statewide leadership.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/ca93b168ab36/c2y1sg9w12-10123189?e=f59034ca3e)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/AI8IR4z0pBJ?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| | | | | | Hi Peter,

A few months ago, I was talking with my friend Sydney about running for the Black Earth Village Board. I knew that her energy and ideas would strengthen our village. And I am so thankful that she decided to take the leap and run for office.
Today, she serves on the board and chairs our Economic Development Committee. In this new role, she helped organize Black Earth's very first Night Market. Neighbors came together to support local businesses, connect with one another, and celebrate our community.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/i8D1fGnqpvL?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| |

Sydney’s story is a perfect example of something I strongly believe in: when we invest in young leaders, our communities become stronger.
I've seen it throughout my own life. I first ran for office in my early twenties because I wanted to help my hometown. Since then, I’ve served on my local school board and village board, led our EMS district, and fought for a more transparent and accountable government.
I could not have done any of this without the people who believed in me. Now, I'm asking Wisconsin to believe in a new generation of statewide leadership.
I'm running for State Treasurer because I know public service can work better when it's transparent, accountable, and focused on helping people understand how their government works.
[But building a statewide campaign takes resources, and unlike many campaigns, we're powered by grassroots supporters giving what they can. If you believe Wisconsin is stronger when every generation has a seat at the table, will you chip in today?](https://us.list-manage.com/1BWUeI8eN5D?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
Every contribution helps us reach more voters, travel to more communities, and continue building a campaign that's powered by people across the state.
Thank you for believing in this campaign and in the next generation of Wisconsin leadership!
Thank you,Dylan

Folks, it’s James Carville.
I’ve spent nearly half a century helping Democrats win elections, and I’m gonna tell you something plainly:
For too long, we have waited until the house was already on fire before deciding to buy a hose.
We wait until a race becomes a crisis.
We wait until a great candidate is getting buried in attack ads.
We wait until Republicans have already built the infrastructure, raised the money, and defined the battlefield.
Then everybody starts running around asking what happened.
Well, Raja Krishnamoorthi has gone and done something about it.
He founded Equal Opportunity Now to find and support bold leaders and important causes before it’s too late — leaders who will stand up to Donald Trump and the MAGA movement, fight for working families, and actually deliver results.
And all I can say is:
FINALLY.
Finally, an organization that understands we cannot defeat MAGA with timid candidates, stale talking points, and a last-minute panic.
But Raja cannot build this by himself.
Will you contribute $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Equal Opportunity Now and another great organization, Resist Reclaim Rebuild, find, fund, and support the leaders Democrats need to start winning again? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
CHIP IN TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
Now, I know Raja.
He is smart. He is tough. And he knows firsthand what opportunity can mean.
His family came to this country with very little. They relied on public housing and food stamps. He worked his way from Peoria all the way to Congress.
And instead of pulling the ladder up behind him, Raja has spent his career fighting to make sure the next family gets the same shot.
That means standing up for workers.
Holding powerful corporations and corrupt politicians accountable.
Defending immigrants, voting rights, and every American targeted by Trump’s politics of division.
And now he is putting that experience toward building the next generation of Democratic leadership.
Here’s the truth: The leaders we need are already out there.
They are running for city council, state legislature, Congress, and offices most national donors are not paying attention to yet.
They have the courage.
They have the ideas.
What they do not always have is the money, infrastructure, and early support necessary to compete.
That is where Equal Opportunity Now and Resist Reclaim Rebuild come in.
Please chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help EON and Resist Reclaim Rebuild form the organization Democrats should have built years ago.
[CLICK HERE TO DONATE NOW >>] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
We’ve got a good battle plan, now, let’s help Raja build this damn thing.
-- James Carville

Dear Friend,
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)I want to tell you something I don't talk about often. A few years ago, federal agents showed up at my home before sunrise. They took my phones. They went through my life. My "crime" was doing journalism the powerful didn't like. I stood outside in the cold and watched it happen, and I'll admit it — for a moment, I wondered if it was finally over. **It wasn't. I'm still here. And I want you to understand why.** [****](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**[STAND WITH ME TODAY — DONATE NOW →](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** I didn't come from money or connections. When I started out, I was funding investigations on credit cards and prayers, driving through the night, certain that if I could just get the truth on tape, people would care. My very first big story brought down a national organization that was caught on hidden camera coaching me how to break the law. Overnight I learned two things that have never left me: the truth on video is the most powerful force in politics — and the people it exposes will spend everything they have to destroy whoever filmed it. **They've tried.** For more than fifteen years they've sued me, smeared me, arrested me, raided me. They even pushed me out of the organization I built with my own hands — a betrayal that nearly broke me. I've lost friends. I've lost sleep. I've signed the front of a paycheck not knowing if there'd be money in the account to cover it. **And I would do all of it again tomorrow.** Because here is what I've learned that I need you to hear: the corrupt are not afraid of articles. They're not afraid of opinions. They are afraid of exactly one thing — getting caught on camera saying what they really mean, and then having to answer for it in front of millions of people. That fear is the only thing that keeps them honest. **And almost no one in America is still willing to create it.** I am. **[But I can't do it alone, and I was never meant to.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** This was never just my fight. It's ours. Every time they raided me, sued me, or counted me out, it wasn't a lawyer who saved this work — it was ordinary Americans who refused to let the truth be buried. **[People like you, who decided that someone has to be willing to pay the price so the rest of the country can stay free.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** I'll keep paying my part. The arrests, the lawsuits, the threats — that's mine to carry. **[All I ask is that you carry yours: help me keep the cameras rolling.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** [**Will you stand with me again today?**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
In Truth,James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group
P.S. ****They thought a dawn raid would scare me into silence. Instead it taught me how badly they want this work to stop — which is exactly how I know it matters.[**Help me make sure it never does.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

clean_body: The honest story of why I can't walk away from this. The honest story of why I can't walk away from this. | Dear Friend, want to tell you something I don't talk about often. A few years ago, federal agents showed up at my home before sunrise. They took my phones. They went through my life. My "crime" was doing journalism the powerful didn't like. I stood outside in the cold and watched it happen, and I'll admit it — for a moment, I wondered if it was finally over. It wasn't. I'm still here. And I want you to understand why. I didn't come from money or connections. When I started out, I was funding investigations on credit cards and prayers, driving through the night, certain that if I could just get the truth on tape, people would care. My very first big story brought down a national organization that was caught on hidden camera coaching me how to break the law. Overnight I learned two things that have never left me: the truth on video is the most powerful force in politics — and the people it exposes will spend everything they have to destroy whoever filmed it. They've tried. For more than fifteen years they've sued me, smeared me, arrested me, raided me. They even pushed me out of the organization I built with my own hands — a betrayal that nearly broke me. I've lost friends. I've lost sleep. I've signed the front of a paycheck not knowing if there'd be money in the account to cover it. And I would do all of it again tomorrow. Because here is what I've learned that I need you to hear: the corrupt are not afraid of articles. They're not afraid of opinions. They are afraid of exactly one thing — getting caught on camera saying what they really mean, and then having to answer for it in front of millions of people. That fear is the only thing that keeps them honest. And almost no one in America is still willing to create it. I am. This was never just my fight. It's ours. Every time they raided me, sued me, or counted me out, it wasn't a lawyer who saved this work — it was ordinary Americans who refused to let the truth be buried. I'll keep paying my part. The arrests, the lawsuits, the threats — that's mine to carry. In Truth,James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. **They thought a dawn raid would scare me into silence. Instead it taught me how badly they want this work to stop — which is exactly how I know it matters.

clean_body: The radical left spends all summer building toward one goal: taking back the House. | Fellow American, Normally, I make my case and then ask. Today I am flipping it. Done? Good. Now here is why it was worth asking before I explained. The radical left spends all summer building toward one goal: taking back the House. And they have already told us exactly what they will do the moment they get it. Impeach President Trump, again, then come after his cabinet one by one. Bury this administration in endless investigations. And freeze the entire America First agenda in its tracks. Most Republicans wait until the fall to fight back, and by then the damage is done. I am not most Republicans. I fight in July, in August, in the months nobody is watching, because that is when elections are actually decided.
