body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/nina2027 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/nina2027]
Hi Friend,
I hope this email finds you healthy, hopeful, and enjoying your summer! 2026 has been full of work and wins in the run-up to Philadelphia's momentous summer celebrating the FIFA World Cup, the MLB All Star Game, and our Nation’s 250th Birthday Celebration.
I wanted to update you on a few current issues that I have been hard at work addressing and to ask for your feedback. Your voice is essential to my ability to find solutions to the problems Philadelphia faces. I want to hear your thoughts and ideas.
First, I continue to lead work with partners like the Enon Baptist Tabernacle Church, Salvation Army, and the Philadelphia Anti-Trafficking Coalition - to prevent and bring awareness to the realities of human trafficking in Philadelphia. I am thrilled to shared that I secured $500,000 in the FY26 budget for the Campaign and that it is in action today.
This Campaign creates a unified citywide response to human trafficking , survivor-informed training [https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/philadelphia-human-trafficking-awareness/] and messaging for City workforce, consistent public awareness tools, aligned data and shared insights, and long-term collaboration across sectors. So far, we have trained nearly 2,000 front-line City employees and created a virtual training to be used by City agencies; provided, for the first time ever, ten dedicated beds for survivors of human trafficking, and created informative videos for distribution to the public.
I was successful in passing a bill to protect survivors of human trafficking from workplace discrimination . Survivors should never be further punished [https://www.instagram.com/p/DT0s9sND6zU/] for what they have endured and deserve dignity and a fair chance to move forward with their lives.
This year, I also passed a Bill to protect immigrants that are survivors of crime and trafficking [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/philadelphia/nina-ahmad-visa-bill-immigrant-council-20260409.html] . My legislation establishes basic guidelines for U-Visa and T-Visa certification requests including requiring timely response to an application, written explanation for denials, limits denial based on the amount of time passed since the crime occurred, and protections against applicants’ immigration status being shared without their consent. U-Visas and T-Visas provide federal immigration protections for crime victims and trafficking survivors and my legislation ensures applicants experience a more transparent, communicative, and timely process [https://www.phillytrib.com/news/local_news/philly-councilwomans-bill-protecting-immigrant-victims-clears-committee-hurdle/article_58f7ad4e-90ea-4df7-813c-64705712594f.html] .
I am also very proud to have lifted up and advocated for the critical role Philadelphia Sexual Assault Response Center (PSARC) has in protecting survivors of sexual violence and making our city safer. This is the only dedicated facility in our city providing forensic medical examinations to survivors ages 16+, operating twenty-four hours per day, seven days per week, and dispatching Sexual Assault Nurse Examiners to its centralized location and to Philadelphia trauma hospitals. My advocacy led to PSARC receiving $300,000 from Mayor Parker and being moved from Drexel University to being housed by the Philadelphia Department of Public Health. I am hopeful that this critical agency will experience more stable funding and oversight and that this new stage in their work brings positive results for all survivors of sexual violence and those who serve them.
I am also thrilled to share that my legislation to establish a permanent Philadelphia Child Welfare Commission [https://www.phillyvoice.com/city-council-proposed-child-welfare-commission/] is moving forward to be placed on the ballot for citywide election , so that voters have the final word. This Commission is a permanent, independent body empowered to advise both City agencies and City Council, bringing accountability and transparency to the systems that serve children and families in Philadelphia. The Commission will work to bridge the gap between the Department of Human Services policies and the realities faced by children and families, and it will do so in the open, on the public record, and with a duty to report what it finds.
I hope you will also stay tuned this fall as I host a tour around Philadelphia to prepare employees and employers as my legislation passed in 2025 that prohibits workplace discrimination against employees experiencing menstruation, perimenopause, or menopause takes effect next year . Menopause, perimenopause, and menstruation are daily realities for a large share of our workforce and my Bill seeks to normalize the lived experience of all workers and to create an equitable workplace where we can all thrive.
Please also check out my 6abc Philly Proud Community Award during AAPI month HERE [https://6abc.com/post/2026-6abc-philly-proud-community-leader-awards-celebrating-aapi-month/19264620/] and my discussion on WURD with Dr. James Peterson about the Philly budget [https://soundcloud.com/onwurd/councilwoman-dr-nina-ahmad-on?si=7a8a893e4aed4b66833cced722f55064&utm_source=clipboard&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=social_sharing] .
As always, I thank you for remaining engaged with my work and your community. Please let me know your thoughts. I look forward to hearing more from you and ask for your continued partnership in the hard work of improving the lives of every Philadelphian. I know that we can do this together!
Thank you again,
Councilmember Nina Ahmad

clean_body: This has been Trump’s playbook since forever | = Hey Peter, Pennsylvania is home to one of the nation’s largest Haitian communities and right now they are under attack. | Across the U.S., about 330,000 Haitian TPS holders keep our neighborhoods, schools, and workplaces running while worrying whether they can stay here with their families. When Trump unilaterally canceled TPS protections for Haitians, he put hundreds of thousands in trouble. This has been Trump’s playbook since forever — disparage and vilify Black communities — but now he is yielding the National Guard and ICE as his own personal paramilitary. We will not forget Daphy Michel, found dead in Pittsburgh from ICE brutality. ICE cruelty kidnapped Daphy Michel from Charleroi and when they could no longer detain her, they dumped her in Pittsburgh alone at a bus stop and she froze to death. | This moment demands our outrage and it demands power — power to protect Black and brown, and immigrant families at the frontlines of Trump’s inhumane agenda and to hold Trump and his administration accountable. Here’s where we hold the power in our hands. The U.S. Senate can check Trump and reinstate TPS protections for Haiti, and Pennsylvania Senators Fetterman and McCormick work for us. When constituents make their concerns loud enough, Senators have to pay attention. | If you are devastated and furious about what happened to Daphy Michel, channel that into building something strong and lasting for our communities. Join us in action. In solidarity, One PA P.S. Please forward this email to three friends and family to make our demands loud and clear. Peter,

Brian Heywood, a billionaire who doesn’t want to pay his fair share, just
came after me.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260713.bzaWdB&refcode=em20260713-6460&t=1002&akid=6460%2E420207%2ElRobis ]A tweet from Pramila that reads "A Republican hedge fund billionaire
who doesn't want to pay his fair share just attacked me personally. Brian
Heywood is the same bully currently spending millions on two WA state
ballot initiatives designed to out LGBTQ+ kids at school and force
invasive exams on every girl who wants to play sports. Oh, and he's also
bankrolling the effort to overturn Washington's millionaires tax. He
didn't come to Washington to build a stronger state. He came to protect
his wealth—and he's using division and fear to do it. He picked the wrong
fight. He is using an old playbook: pit people against each other so
billionaires can keep the rules rigged in their favor. Washington has
beaten him before. Doctors, teachers, nurses, parents, athletes, Planned
Parenthood, and the WEA are already organized. The coalition is built. Now
we need all of you."

That’s not surprising. I’ve spent my career fighting for working people,
defending LGBTQ+ communities, and taking on the powerful interests trying
to divide us.

The same people bankrolling attacks on our rights and our democracy want
politicians who will stay quiet.

I’m not one of them.

Congress is supposed to provide a check and balance. On tariffs that are driving up costs for our farmers and small businesses. On a war in the Middle East that is costing billions of dollars, while gas prices stay above four dollars a gallon. Andy Ogles has not done any of that. He has been a rubber stamp his entire career, and this district has paid the price for it.

body:
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135209785/633466313/938567526?refcode=header&noskip=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2ZiNTJmMy1mZDdlLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EJVhxeA5bKU5c13GwIca9TX1eJTKSlwVsrmC3Fk78xA=)
Folks,
Across Los Angeles County neighbors are reporting increased immigration enforcement, with several incidents documented and shared on social media.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135209786/633466314/789508428?refcode=260713_RG_ICE_em&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2ZiNTJmMy1mZDdlLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EJVhxeA5bKU5c13GwIca9TX1eJTKSlwVsrmC3Fk78xA=)
People are being stopped, questioned, and detained in the middle of their daily lives. Workers are afraid to go to their jobs. Parents are worried about picking up their kids. Entire neighborhoods are being forced to live on edge.
**This doesn't make anyone safer. It creates fear and chaos in our communities.**
**Trump wants people to feel powerless. He wants families to stay silent while ICE expands its presence _across Los Angeles._**
_I refuse to let that happen._
I’m fighting in Congress to hold ICE accountable, defend due process, and stop this administration from treating immigrant families like political targets.

Today I’m leading a coalition of 12 states in filing a new federal lawsuit to block the largest merger in Hollywood history.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/91260/images/Screenshot%202026-07-13%20at%203.14.21%E2%80%AFPM.png]
The film industry is incredibly important to California, so I want to talk through exactly what this merger would mean — and why we’re asking the court to step in and block it:
Paramount Skydance is already massive. If their merger with Warner Bros. Discovery goes through, one industry titan would own two of Hollywood’s major film distributors and two of the major basic cable channel owners.
The combined corporation would control nearly one-third of all theatrical motion pictures, and nearly one-third of basic cable TV programming — a clear violation of antitrust law.
If you want to support our work enforcing antitrust law and holding powerful corporations accountable to the law, please contribute any amount today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
With this merger, Paramount and Warner Bros. would be able to snuff out competition, drive up prices, diminish content quality, and create fewer films and television shows each year.
We have antitrust laws for a reason: competition fuels innovation. Think of Titanic, The Godfather, Casablanca, Harry Potter ... who knows what these movies would have been like if not for the competition driving these distributors to produce their very best work?
The film industry has the power to bring us together, and in California it's a source of immense pride — and employment — up and down the state. The industry exists to tell stories, to spark ideas and curiosity, to inspire and inform, and to open our eyes to new perspectives.
It doesn’t exist to create monopolies that drive up prices and drive down consumer choice.
I’m suing Paramount and Warner Bros. to block this merger, make sure antitrust laws are enforced, and protect consumers in California and across the country.
If you’re with me, will you help power our work with a contribution right now? No amount is too small — anything you can give has a real impact on what we can accomplish together. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

| | Dear Faithful Friend,
This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question: _**Are we keeping the faith?** _
Let me explain what I mean.
At the very heart of it, _we were born a nation of Christian pilgrims and dissenters. _
The Pilgrims. The Puritans. The Quakers. The Huguenots. The German Pietists. Wave after wave of men and women who crossed an ocean because they refused to let any earthly power stand between them and their biblical faith in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the God revealed in Jesus Christ.
_That is the seed America grew from_ , and every time we’ve forgotten this, we’ve gone astray.
The very first freedom in the Bill of Rights – the one the framers put first, not fifth or tenth, but first – is **the freedom to worship God without interference from government**. That wasn’t random. It was the whole point.
And when people knock our founding fathers as relics of a bygone era who “wouldn’t understand the world today,” I ask you to think about our brothers and sisters in Christ today, _right now_ , in places like Nigeria, Iran, Pakistan, North Korea and many other places.
**There are an estimated 388 million Christian men, women and children being persecuted, oppressed and ruthlessly murdered simply for loving Jesus.**
Here in America, _it’s almost impossible to know what that’s like_ , but we do have the freedom, the platform and the resources to support them, and fight back in a wide range of ways. **The question is, will we?**
I can’t help but feel that this year, on the 250th birthday of the world’s most indispensable Christian nation, that we have a duty to rededicate ourselves to God and to the defense of His people around the world. **And today, I’m asking you to partner with me and an incredible organization in that endeavor.**
**There is no organization in this country more committed to that fight than Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member.** ** ** Whether it’s the growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America, it is due in very large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide.

As you contemplate your potential commitment, I ask you to think about this.
**While Christians in America today are the freest Christians in the history of the world, 388 million of our brothers and sisters, in other parts of the world, are being hunted for practicing the same faith that built this country.**
Every generation that ever mattered to the kingdom of God understood that faith without action is sentiment – and sentiment has never freed a single soul.
**Now it's our turn.**
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. _They paid the price._ They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it.
On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail.
He told her this new American holiday " _ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more._ "
Notice the order. _First solemn devotion to God._ Then the fireworks.
250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion?
I believe we still can. **This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning** – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly.
They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names.

clean_body: This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question | | | | | | | | | Dear Faithful Friend, This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question: Are we keeping the faith? Let me explain what I mean. At the very heart of it, we were born a nation of Christian pilgrims and dissenters. The Pilgrims. The Puritans. The Quakers. The Huguenots. The German Pietists. Wave after wave of men and women who crossed an ocean because they refused to let any earthly power stand between them and their biblical faith in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the God revealed in Jesus Christ. That is the seed America grew from , and every time we’ve forgotten this, we’ve gone astray. The very first freedom in the Bill of Rights – the one the framers put first, not fifth or tenth, but first – is the freedom to worship God without interference from government. That wasn’t random. It was the whole point. And when people knock our founding fathers as relics of a bygone era who “wouldn’t understand the world today,” I ask you to think about our brothers and sisters in Christ today, right now , in places like Nigeria, Iran, Pakistan, North Korea and many other places. There are an estimated 388 million Christian men, women and children being persecuted, oppressed and ruthlessly murdered simply for loving Jesus. Here in America, it’s almost impossible to know what that’s like , but we do have the freedom, the platform and the resources to support them, and fight back in a wide range of ways. The question is, will we? I can’t help but feel that this year, on the 250th birthday of the world’s most indispensable Christian nation, that we have a duty to rededicate ourselves to God and to the defense of His people around the world. And today, I’m asking you to partner with me and an incredible organization in that endeavor. There is no organization in this country more committed to that fight than Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member. Whether it’s the growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America, it is due in very large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide. | "MAKE A GIFT TODAY" As you contemplate your potential commitment, I ask you to think about this. While Christians in America today are the freest Christians in the history of the world, 388 million of our brothers and sisters, in other parts of the world, are being hunted for practicing the same faith that built this country. Every generation that ever mattered to the kingdom of God understood that faith without action is sentiment – and sentiment has never freed a single soul. Now it's our turn. Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. They paid the price. They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it. On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail. He told her this new American holiday " ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more. " Notice the order. First solemn devotion to God. Then the fireworks. 250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion? I believe we still can. This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly. They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names. On this 250th birthday – of all years – we have the chance to tell them they are not forgotten. Thank you for your time, your patriotism, and your commitment. For God and country, Eric Metaxas Member, Board of Directors Save the Persecuted Christians | | | "SAVE CHRISTIANS" | | | | | | | | Save the Persecuted Christians PO Box 543 Monument, CO 80132 USA

This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question: _**Are we keeping the faith?** _
Let me explain what I mean.
At the very heart of it, _we were born a nation of Christian pilgrims and dissenters. _
The Pilgrims. The Puritans. The Quakers. The Huguenots. The German Pietists. Wave after wave of men and women who crossed an ocean because they refused to let any earthly power stand between them and their biblical faith in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the God revealed in Jesus Christ.
_That is the seed America grew from_ , and every time we’ve forgotten this, we’ve gone astray.
The very first freedom in the Bill of Rights – the one the framers put first, not fifth or tenth, but first – is **the freedom to worship God without interference from government**. That wasn’t random. It was the whole point.
And when people knock our founding fathers as relics of a bygone era who “wouldn’t understand the world today,” I ask you to think about our brothers and sisters in Christ today, _right now_ , in places like Nigeria, Iran, Pakistan, North Korea and many other places.

Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. They paid the price. They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it. On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail. He told her this new American holiday " ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more. " Notice the order. First solemn devotion to God. Then the fireworks. 250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion? I believe we still can. This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly. They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names. On this 250th birthday – of all years – we have the chance to tell them they are not forgotten. Thank you for your time, your patriotism, and your commitment. For God and country, Eric Metaxas Member, Board of Directors Save the Persecuted Christians | | | "SAVE CHRISTIANS" | | | | | | | | Save the Persecuted Christians PO Box 543 Monument, CO 80132 USA

Team, I've been using this analogy a lot on the campaign trail: **The government is like a hammer. It can be used to build things, or it can be used to break things. It all depends on who's holding it.** For decades, that hammer built things most of us never think twice about. It built the research that eradicated deadly diseases and helped improve crop production. It built the safety nets like Social Security and Medicare that keep families from falling through the cracks. It built the agencies that make sure we have clean water to drink and safe air to breathe. Right now, that same hammer is being used to break things that took generations to build. Trump and DOGE have gutted the federal agencies and workforce that serve us, defunded the scientific and biomedical research that protects us, and dismantled programs that keep us safe from wildfires and floods – all under the guise of “government efficiency.” **That's not efficiency. That's demolition.** As a scientist, I know what it takes to build solutions to our problems. As a teacher, I know what it takes to build a kid's future and opportunities to thrive. As a public servant in the U.S. Senate, NIH, and GAO, I know what it takes to build a government that works for everyday people instead of special interests. clean_body: The government is like a hammer | | = Team, I've been using this analogy a lot on the campaign trail: The government is like a hammer. It can be used to build things, or it can be used to break things. It all depends on who's holding it. For decades, that hammer built things most of us never think twice about. It built the research that eradicated deadly diseases and helped improve crop production. It built the safety nets like Social Security and Medicare that keep families from falling through the cracks. It built the agencies that make sure we have clean water to drink and safe air to breathe. Right now, that same hammer is being used to break things that took generations to build. Trump and DOGE have gutted the federal agencies and workforce that serve us, defunded the scientific and biomedical research that protects us, and dismantled programs that keep us safe from wildfires and floods – all under the guise of “government efficiency.” That's not efficiency. That's demolition. As a scientist, I know what it takes to build solutions to our problems. As a teacher, I know what it takes to build a kid's future and opportunities to thrive. As a public servant in the U.S. Senate, NIH, and GAO, I know what it takes to build a government that works for everyday people instead of special interests. When I’m in Washington, I will pick up the hammer to build – not just for my community in TX-21, but for all communities. = | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately. name: Ro Khanna
subject: I will not be silenced about what I saw in Palestine.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ro for Congress
body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
I just returned from Palestine, where I spent several days meeting with families about the daily realities of life under occupation.
https://x.com/RoKhanna/status/2076675686916354109 [https://x.com/RoKhanna/status/2076675686916354109]
While visiting a Palestinian school that had been burned down by settlers, my staff and I were surrounded by armed settlers carrying American-made M4 rifles. They blocked our vehicle, called in reinforcements, mocked us, and held us against our will for more than an hour.
When Israeli soldiers arrived, I expected them to stop the settlers. Instead, they protected them.
I was eventually allowed to leave because I'm an American member of Congress. Millions of Palestinians don't have that privilege.
If violent settlers and the Israeli military could do this to an American congressman, imagine what Palestinian families endure every day—with no cameras, no headlines, and no one to speak up for them.
Throughout this trip, I met people who had lost loved ones, been driven from their land, and were struggling for the most basic human rights: safety, freedom of movement, and the dignity to live in peace.
For too long, their voices have been ignored.
There must be consequences for violent extremism and continued settlement expansion.
* Designate the Hilltop Youth as a terrorist group,
* Prosecute violent settlers like Yinon Levy, and
* Halt all settlement construction in the occupied West Bank
Will you join me and demand that the United States take action to urge Israel to act? [https://act.rokhanna.com/a/idf-hilltop-youth-petition?contactdata=F/8LlMmdp0RvP7XHh7BugLn5VPBjJP7kO/lCJBRDl9fPJc3X9joVd43yl+uagkC1+WcJ0QAumHnFPf/mq8NCH3QE0s8e1NY8b7qSK9IN1eWxC3Kg4si96iikre+2OcvzAyEzXz1Y+qc9S70aPo0vb3qg/UuzwLhrBzZ/qUpt6oY8VEwA1HHzSmICaC1ZNKh+]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://act.rokhanna.com/a/idf-hilltop-youth-petition?contactdata=F/8LlMmdp0RvP7XHh7BugLn5VPBjJP7kO/lCJBRDl9fPJc3X9joVd43yl+uagkC1+WcJ0QAumHnFPf/mq8NCH3QE0s8e1NY8b7qSK9IN1eWxC3Kg4si96iikre+2OcvzAyEzXz1Y+qc9S70aPo0vb3qg/UuzwLhrBzZ/qUpt6oY8VEwA1HHzSmICaC1ZNKh+]
I won't be silenced about what I witnessed in Palestine. I'll continue sharing the stories I heard over the coming weeks because Americans deserve to know what is happening. But today, I'm asking you to stand with people who are simply demanding equal rights, accountability, and the chance to live with dignity.
Thank you for your support, your activism, and all that you do.
Onward,
Ro

clean_body: [] Peter, I just returned from Palestine, where I spent several days meeting with families about the daily realities of life under occupation. [] While visiting a Palestinian school that had been burned down by settlers, my staff and I were surrounded by armed settlers carrying American-made M4 rifles. They blocked our vehicle, called in reinforcements, mocked us, and held us against our will for more than an hour. When Israeli soldiers arrived, I expected them to stop the settlers. Instead, they protected them. I was eventually allowed to leave because I'm an American member of Congress. Millions of Palestinians don't have that privilege. If violent settlers and the Israeli military could do this to an American congressman, imagine what Palestinian families endure every day—with no cameras, no headlines, and no one to speak up for them. Throughout this trip, I met people who had lost loved ones, been driven from their land, and were struggling for the most basic human rights: safety, freedom of movement, and the dignity to live in peace. For too long, their voices have been ignored. There must be consequences for violent extremism and continued settlement expansion. Designate the Hilltop Youth as a terrorist group, Prosecute violent settlers like Yinon Levy, and * Halt all settlement construction in the occupied West Bank Will you join me and demand that the United States take action to urge Israel to act? [+] ADD YOUR NAME [+] I won't be silenced about what I witnessed in Palestine. I'll continue sharing the stories I heard over the coming weeks because Americans deserve to know what is happening. But today, I'm asking you to stand with people who are simply demanding equal rights, accountability, and the chance to live with dignity. Thank you for your support, your activism, and all that you do. Onward, Ro Wait! One more thing– Ro doesn't accept a cent from lobbyists or PACs, meaning our work is completely funded by grassroots supporters like you. By donating just $3 today, you’re helping us create a country that works for everyone, not just those at the top. That means a renewed investment in American manufacturing, Medicare for All, student debt relief, and a green future. If you want to support our people-powered campaign as we continue to fight for progress in Washington, please consider making a donation of $3 or more today. Thank you! Building political power at the state level is just as important.
#
Peter,
This year, Voto Latino is going all-in across 9 competitive states and 22 critical battleground districts to flip the U.S. House.
But building true political power doesn't stop with the House and Senate. We’re also focusing on governor’s races that will shape our communities at the state level.
**Right now, we’re zeroing in on the high-stakes race for Georgia governor.**
Former Atlanta Mayor **Keisha Lance Bottoms is the Democratic nominee for governor.** And if she’s elected this fall, she will make history as the first Democratic Governor of Georgia elected this century.
We can break the conservative grip on Georgia, but we can’t get across the finish line without a voter registration push and voter turnout efforts.
[**With this in mind, will you pitch in $3 right now to help power our voter registration efforts in Georgia and help elect Keisha Lance Bottoms this November?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260713-1.ZRA4sn&amount=3&refcode=em20260713-371&t=1&akid=371%2E1366028%2EHQvm4C)
Latino voters will be the absolute margin of victory in this race, Peter. **Georgia’s Latino electorate has surged to _498,298 registered voters_ , representing a critical 4.1% of the state's total voting population.**
The data also shows that 64% of Georgia Latinos voted for Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024, proving that Latino voters remain the most decisive factor for any statewide campaign.
Our community has the unique power to elect a leader like Keisha Lance Bottoms and completely reshape Georgia's future. By showing up at full strength, we have the power to protect voting rights, stop extreme agendas at the state level, and flip Georgia.
But we can only win this seat if we register every single eligible voter on the sidelines and make sure they show up at the ballot box this November.

Friend, ICE has shot and killed another person in Maine today, ripping a life away from yet another family and traumatizing yet another community with senseless, fascist violence.
A so-far unnamed 26-year-old was shot six times in his car by ICE agents, despite being in the country with a legal and valid work status.

When ICE agents got away with murdering Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti in my city just months ago, it sent a clear message from the administration: If you hurt and kill innocent people, we will stand by you. We will not investigate you. You will not be held accountable.
**Trump, JD Vance, Stephen Miller, and the whole corrupt fascist crew gave ICE and Border Patrol a practical license to kill.** As long as they carry out Trump’s mass deportation agenda, they are above the law.
We should be beyond outraged that we must live in fear of our government. That so many have been killed, hurt, tortured, abused, and had their rights violated.
We need to abolish ICE. We need to block any more funding for DHS in Congress. And we need to hold these federal agents criminally responsible for their violent lawlessness.

* * *
It's been a little over 24 hours since we all woke up and learned that Lindsey Graham -- not Mitch McConnell -- had died overnight. And I keep turning that sentence over in my head because it says everything about where we are right now: a sitting United States senator died, and half the country's first reaction was... _wait, which one!?_
That's a surreal feeling. When someone who's been a fixture in American politics for decades -- whether you liked Graham or not, and mostly I didn't -- is just suddenly gone, it rattles something loose. So consider this my messy, raw reaction to a genuinely weird week in our politics.
Let me state a few things up front. I believe the reporting that Graham died of an aortic dissection. It tracks with his age and his lifestyle. The same thing nearly killed my grandfather. But I want to be equally clear about this: I am not judging anyone who's questioning the official story. Not after the way they've handled McConnell. Not after Epstein. Not after everything else. When you lie mercilessly about everything, all the time, you don't get to act shocked when people stop believing you -- you invited this. At this point, questioning your government isn't paranoia. It's basically your patriotic duty because your government, it seems, is lying to you about freaking everything.
But here's the thing: Graham's death didn't happen in a vacuum. It happened in week four of the Mitch McConnell disappearance -- and yes, I'm calling it a disappearance because that's what it is. We haven't seen the man in a month. They released a photo yesterday that created more questions than it answered. We've had the obviously fake phone calls. The alleged remodel at the house. His wife not flying home after he went into cardiac arrest and was found lying lifeless on the ground. None of it adds up, and everyone can see that none of it adds up, and nobody with any power seems interested in making it add up. Although I appreciated Governor Beshear saying over the weekend that he intends to appoint a Democrat to replace McConnell, defying the state legislature.
And look -- I don't know exactly what's going on with Mitch McConnell. Maybe it's all innocent, and he'll be up and back to work soon. I doubt it. But I know what it looks like, and I know that we shouldn't have to squint at hostage-style photos of an 84-year-old Senate leader, trying to figure out if he's alive.
* * *

* * *
Here's the number that should make everyone furious: the average member of Congress is 68 years old. The average American is 38. We are being governed by people who are, on average, 30 years older than the country they represent. And that gap isn't an abstraction -- it produces exactly the outcomes you'd expect. It produces Dianne Feinstein dying in office. It produces Chuck Grassley running for reelection into his 90s. It produces members of Congress who literally vanish for weeks and months at a time -- one of whom, we later learned, had been moved into an assisted living facility for dementia. Another disappeared for four months because he was depressed.
And let me be clear about that last one because I don't want to be misread: depression is real. I've dealt with it myself. It's brutal. And my problem is not that he got the care he needed -- he should have gotten that care. Everyone should. That's actually the whole point.
Because this same guy voted to cut mental health funding in the Republican budget. His party has spent years trying to gut Medicare and Medicaid -- the programs that would let ordinary Americans get the exact kind of help he quietly gave himself. And here's the part that really gets me: he apparently wasn't too depressed to keep insider trading. Too sick to show up for work, but well enough to abuse his office to make money for himself.
That's the two-tiered system in practice. If you're a powerful member of Congress, if you know the right person, if you put enough money in somebody's back pocket, you get treated entirely differently in this country. You get four months off and a soft landing. Meanwhile, the rest of us are stuck with gravity. When I was going through my own stuff, I still had to show up to work every day because if I hadn't, there would have been consequences -- for my clients, my business, my family. Regular people who get sick and run out of sick days lose their jobs. That's it. That's the deal for everyone who isn't them. And I just think that's fucked up.
There are no consequences for these people. None. They can disappear. They can lie about it. They can cover it up. They can cheat, they can steal, they can trade stocks based on information you and I will never see, and nothing happens. Donald Trump is the ultimate personification of this -- the living proof that if you're powerful enough in this country, accountability is optional. But he didn't invent the rot. He's just the loudest symptom of it.
The strange thing about living through something that fundamentally changes you--whether it's depression, serious illness, or coming face-to-face with your own mortality--is that an old version of you has to disappear before a better one has the chance to exist. I know that was true for me. You come out the other side realizing how temporary everything is, how fragile we all are, and how much more important helping and healing each other is than winning the next political argument. Maybe that's the bigger story this week. Nothing lasts forever--not people, not power, not political movements--and that's not always something to fear.
Sometimes the things that are no longer serving us have to come to an end before something healthier can take their place. I think that's true for people just as much as it's true for countries. As this generation of Congress gives way to the next, I don't think we're just watching individual lives change. I think we're watching an entire political era reach the end of its natural life.
Generational change is coming to America whether anyone in Washington wants it or not. Time comes for us all. Time is coming for Donald Trump. Time is coming for Bibi Netanyahu. Time came for Lindsey Graham this week, and it appears to be trying -- and so far failing -- to come for Mitch McConnell. You cannot fundraise your way out of it. You cannot gerrymander it. You cannot release a carefully cropped photo and make it go away.
I won't pretend I know that what comes next will be better. History doesn't owe us an upgrade. But I know this era of American politics -- the gerontocracy, the consequence-free ruling class, the pretending this is all okay -- is coming to a close. And it's not ending with dignity. It's ending like a long, slow, embarrassing, wet fart.
But it is ending. And that means we have a real opportunity -- maybe the biggest one in a generation -- to reset the course of this country in the next presidential election. A new version of the Democratic Party. A new version of the Republican Party. New people, new fights, new stakes. That's the work in front of us, and it's work worth doing.
So that's my takeaway on Lindsey Graham. I'm not going to lionize him. I'm not going to mourn him, either. He was a man who worked relentlessly for things I spent my career fighting against, and now he's gone, and the era he belonged to is going with him.
Time comes for us all. The only question is what we build before it gets here.

The strange thing about living through something that fundamentally changes you--whether it's depression, serious illness, or coming face-to-face with your own mortality--is that an old version of you has to disappear before a better one has the chance to exist. I know that was true for me. You come out the other side realizing how temporary everything is, how fragile we all are, and how much more important helping and healing each other is than winning the next political argument. Maybe that's the bigger story this week. Nothing lasts forever--not people, not power, not political movements--and that's not always something to fear. Sometimes the things that are no longer serving us have to come to an end before something healthier can take their place. I think that's true for people just as much as it's true for countries. As this generation of Congress gives way to the next, I don't think we're just watching individual lives change. I think we're watching an entire political era reach the end of its natural life. Generational change is coming to America whether anyone in Washington wants it or not. Time comes for us all. Time is coming for Donald Trump. Time is coming for Bibi Netanyahu. Time came for Lindsey Graham this week, and it appears to be trying -- and so far failing -- to come for Mitch McConnell. You cannot fundraise your way out of it. You cannot gerrymander it. You cannot release a carefully cropped photo and make it go away. I won't pretend I know that what comes next will be better. History doesn't owe us an upgrade. But I know this era of American politics -- the gerontocracy, the consequence-free ruling class, the pretending this is all okay -- is coming to a close. And it's not ending with dignity. It's ending like a long, slow, embarrassing, wet fart. But it is ending. And that means we have a real opportunity -- maybe the biggest one in a generation -- to reset the course of this country in the next presidential election. A new version of the Democratic Party. A new version of the Republican Party. New people, new fights, new stakes. That's the work in front of us, and it's work worth doing. So that's my takeaway on Lindsey Graham. I'm not going to lionize him. I'm not going to mourn him, either. He was a man who worked relentlessly for things I spent my career fighting against, and now he's gone, and the era he belonged to is going with him. Time comes for us all. The only question is what we build before it gets here. Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. name: Dan Cox
subject: 16 Saturdays left
body:
We need your help now. | | |
# Only 16 Saturdays to Save Maryland.
---
| | Dear , We want to thank you for all you have and are doing to save Maryland with us. What we cannot do alone, you are helping happen together. **IMPORTANT - please read our PS below as well as this e-mail update.**

We as Republicans in Maryland are united like never before; Wes Moore has awakened us to the need of this hour. **Our children and seniors are questioning a future here in Maryland, businesses and family finances are facing certain overwhelming taxes and fee increases, and our streets are more and more dangerous, only to get worse without change**.

**We literally only have 16 Saturdays until the election on November 3** where we will determine the future of our State. This is why I am personally asking for your help now to do two things:

1\. Sponsor our TV ads now running state-wide on streaming services to over 550 channels such as ESPN, NBC/CBS/ABC, CNN, FoxNews, movie shows, and more. We also need to get our ads on cable. We need at least [10 donors at $400/week](https://us.list-manage.com/185eNllO2ww?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) for the remaining 16 weeks until the election to cover this push. Will you help us?

2\. Sign up to volunteer to door knock with me and our teams across the five bluest counties plus Baltimore City. People are hurting and they realize it's not about Party politics, it is about right policies. When we reach them door to door, they vote for our policies. Sign up today [here](https://us.list-manage.com/RdlqAVg6tY7?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

3\. [Display a sign](https://us.list-manage.com/uqmGHcwvD89?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) and [buy our merch](https://us.list-manage.com/LPndwWFp4pe?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b). We are adding new merchandise weekly - help us out by getting it delivered to your house and displaying them.
Thank you for joining us to fight for our State, Our Beautiful Maryland.

[](https://us.list-manage.com/kRdIa0_D8TU?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)
Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Governor of Maryland
P.S. If you are wondering why I am asking you every day now for help to win, it is because this is the most time sensitive task we have: to raise the funds necessary to save our State and get our excellent TV ads all over streaming, cable and social media platforms reaching millions. Keep in mind it can take 5-7 days to get a TV ad airing once we have shot the commercial, just because of cyclical programming. So this request if acted on today by you will actually matriculate into TV ads likely a week from now at the earliest. So this is why time is of the essence today. Thank you for helping!

Authority: Dan Cox for Governor; Nick Krop, CPA, Treasurer.

---
|
---

## _Join us on the campaign trail to keep the momentum going_
---

**Election Day is now three weeks away. The finish line is in sight. But we can’t stop now—our future depends on us pushing forward.**
**Our team spent the weekend traveling throughout rural communities talking about Elizabeth’s plans to make life better for every resident in this district. We have more exciting events planned this week and we’re excited to invite you to join us.**

subject: Tell the Senate: Vote NO on the NDAA

body:
This budget would give Hegseth and Trump a blank check to wage war with Iran.
#
Peter, this is a strange position for VoteVets to be in.
The National Defense Authorization Act is a traditionally bipartisan bill, and it’s exactly what it sounds like — it funds the Pentagon.
Traditionally bipartisan, until this year. A bill we traditionally support, until now. For two big reasons:
First, Hegseth and Trump want $1.15 trillion dollars for the Pentagon (and they want to pass another $350 billion through budget reconciliation later). That is the largest defense budget ever, by hundreds of billions of dollars. And with Trump in the White House and his kids running the family business, it’s another opportunity for massive, unprecedented grift and corruption.
Trump took one of the last things a divided Congress could agree on — paying the men and women serving in uniform — and destroyed it so he could make a quick buck. It’s a bridge too far. But there’s another important reason we can’t support this NDAA, and it’s bigger than grift alone.
This NDAA would give Hegseth and Trump a blank check to wage war with Iran. Republicans have repeatedly refused to impose ANY guardrails on Trump’s illegal war, but they’re happy to spend hundreds of billions of dollars on it.
It’s cowardice, and an abdication of duty the likes of which we have never seen. VoteVets is against this war. We are against this NDAA. And we need you with us.
[**Please, add your name and demand the Senate vote down this NDAA. Send a message to Trump, Hegseth, and the GOP that the American people will not stand for another illegal forever war.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/260713_VV_war_powers_em/?source=em260713-1-120&refcode2=35337.3013755.GoA1fa&akid=35337%2E3013755%2EGoA1fa)

The earthquakes in Venezuela dominated the news for a matter of days. The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, **the world watched, then largely moved on.** But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. **In some ways, it was only the beginning.** Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. In that broken space, a stranger offering "help," a ride, a promise of safety somewhere else, can be all it takes for a child to disappear.

I've sat with survivors. I've heard what it costs a family to lose a child this way, and what it takes to bring one home. And I've learned that disasters like the one in Venezuela don't create new evil, they simply hand existing evil an opening it has used again and again. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** is to **stop the sale of God's children.** We do that through five pillars:
---
* **Prevention**
* **Intervention**
* **Education**
* **Information**
* **Influence**

---
We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to:
---
* Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster.
* Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety.
* Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free.
* Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified.
* Walk alongside a child through long-term care when there is nowhere safe to send them yet.

| | Dear Faithful Friend,
This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question: _**Are we keeping the faith?** _
Let me explain what I mean.
At the very heart of it, _we were born a nation of Christian pilgrims and dissenters. _
The Pilgrims. The Puritans. The Quakers. The Huguenots. The German Pietists. Wave after wave of men and women who crossed an ocean because they refused to let any earthly power stand between them and their biblical faith in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the God revealed in Jesus Christ.
_That is the seed America grew from_ , and every time we’ve forgotten this, we’ve gone astray.
The very first freedom in the Bill of Rights – the one the framers put first, not fifth or tenth, but first – is **the freedom to worship God without interference from government**. That wasn’t random. It was the whole point.
And when people knock our founding fathers as relics of a bygone era who “wouldn’t understand the world today,” I ask you to think about our brothers and sisters in Christ today, _right now_ , in places like Nigeria, Iran, Pakistan, North Korea and many other places.
**There are an estimated 388 million Christian men, women and children being persecuted, oppressed and ruthlessly murdered simply for loving Jesus.**
Here in America, _it’s almost impossible to know what that’s like_ , but we do have the freedom, the platform and the resources to support them, and fight back in a wide range of ways. **The question is, will we?**
I can’t help but feel that this year, on the 250th birthday of the world’s most indispensable Christian nation, that we have a duty to rededicate ourselves to God and to the defense of His people around the world. **And today, I’m asking you to partner with me and an incredible organization in that endeavor.**
**There is no organization in this country more committed to that fight than Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member.** ** ** Whether it’s the growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America, it is due in very large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide.
[ **As we commemorate America’s 250th birthday, I humbly but urgently ask that you help to supercharge their efforts with a generous, tax-deductible contribution.** ](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=a79d3de7bd7c4536a1aff875a73cf655&_e=bO81Za_ClRn0-QXfgjFUtiCcmumClkP9N9odCKsP0fHgDitihr6uVEIunP1KHTFezpN1AKwJno3OUp6PqA9IRr73d-iMioh0ACQlzvCV0Jz7eqMnCcD18Wcm-9aahyChTBYsFKA3F1BVsikaUiwxVrh9BPuMUWQn1H_TYgYJlnDyxRINqlNYNfUWLQSIm70Yg9KznTuefiWjRMVN1Axv5vQgC-P77NSJbQ28x0nMNXdsOYBFQnwm5g8-6rKCtGVRxpNUVj4ZPIjrYpjzmcP1g7WO8L7hN6F-qBbeFU5L3n9AyCImwQBDscV4q0NcrsaT_3HudUKXst--Pxpdl9NxX4Gb6uxCjfNdKhyoKwXQs6rgduw90B8scHP1zLeTQb21TphFxVCTzSgPHkU8QmZwZ6zwWe6wIt5VO2Z7o-6Pmk_EL0m5hKcaOIibIVj43uJyJz9LgeV1Gwsd54JeNIjB2iHIJ_S-yhhdE8bFnN8Hagq5RgRHN4S0W2aqa_ueW4OWFXet0h6hcTvfxV8UIVetahDeloirhp4WO4qhm9Wh7OPz6djKjZlpBIDBfjiOMhwJtdsQeZTuveCOXyZ0Njc8gTeQEj9qgIz67bpDJgB5DBt1fN_iiLtoZZrFlVCmKxqDRCwhgO9k0c4H0I5whCBuQuNc8vB-Ym76AxMoYi6keQ32AG4HY--FeSORF8F8D5ahIFqAA9TjrlXQew5D7p-Uc5gnuWTW_odiP1nK1n6ckBvXCC9qPBn9BINB6gv8hwJW)

As you contemplate your potential commitment, I ask you to think about this.
**While Christians in America today are the freest Christians in the history of the world, 388 million of our brothers and sisters, in other parts of the world, are being hunted for practicing the same faith that built this country.**
Every generation that ever mattered to the kingdom of God understood that faith without action is sentiment – and sentiment has never freed a single soul.
**Now it's our turn.**
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. _They paid the price._ They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it.
On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail.
He told her this new American holiday " _ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more._ "
Notice the order. _First solemn devotion to God._ Then the fireworks.
250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion?
I believe we still can. **This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning** – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly.
They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names.
On this 250th birthday – of all years – we have the chance to tell them they are not forgotten.
[ **That is what your gift does. That is what Save the Persecuted Christians does. And that is why, I am asking you to give as generously as you possibly can.** ](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=a79d3de7bd7c4536a1aff875a73cf655&_e=bO81Za_ClRn0-QXfgjFUtiCcmumClkP9N9odCKsP0fHgDitihr6uVEIunP1KHTFezpN1AKwJno3OUp6PqA9IRr73d-iMioh0ACQlzvCV0Jz7eqMnCcD18Wcm-9aahyChTBYsFKA3F1BVsikaUiwxVrh9BPuMUWQn1H_TYgYJlnDyxRINqlNYNfUWLQSIm70Yg9KznTuefiWjRMVN1Axv5vQgC-P77NSJbQ28x0nMNXdsOYBFQnwm5g8-6rKCtGVRxpNUVj4ZPIjrYpjzmcP1g23BeDcxEvEp6yTP7koiPb5FSaWMnPdelEx6PzVZhhw0eG8q24EzGM3jFqJYvlnsOtsNB-iue8JXJ-KGEIF8x_LzGoxy-GRI8JLyLnZ69E1RR6FYphJ5G3BQDReR5ZqKzJychliLhGnS732RsCmN7Y6lLIDqEtV85l_h6NtL6cwrjA4Dfwzw3bY3LO4yCONMlryPoQFRgVkqvPlXfb3Hn-F2KgdNiu9IAkCG7Ofpuw7jHrrk345ED601QcbOIHsYkOtQ1JEd7zHnO1eQEyDAIUTOCTJLT3X7a5OlUqgH8bxHSBg-MUxW1x-cpE0IKGpinpNRGV_sIIybpJTWpJ42A99Lr8YeP0A4QJL1ZoHwrAdtTT1m-jGCrbM8cmvEE37zprG6r7wc9CijFJfgc4DfS87LrdPtYyOTd9wuFv5-T3qNIqBKc4tk5wtZuwAVRgTIouWQruJY31POKYNezVd2O7gOLwxuJnnor9jFwlKGnNRi)

| | Good Evening,
Rob spent the 4th of July weekend in every county in the district. He started out in Stroudsburg for their first ever 4th of July parade. He then made his way over to Dallas for the Hometown Heroes America 250 celebration to meet with all of you and the greater Dallas Community. Rob then launched the fireworks at the Backwoods Bar & Kitchen in Dallas to celebrate a great 4th of July.
Thank you to all who showed up and showed out to celebrate America’s 250th birthday!
---
|

---](https://us.list-manage.com/NvcBHlU_Bif?e=131e83a3c2&c2id=e7faf2081078228733221dbd5e122ac9)
|
---
| |
Last week, with the tragic passing of State Trooper Michael Pahira along Interstate 81 in Cass Township, now more than ever we need to see stricter laws to protect Northeastern Pennsylvanians from those who are in our country illegally. Our Congressman has called to discuss Dalilah's Law; a bill that would ban issuance of Commercial Driver’s Licenses to people who are not citizens or lawful residents of this country.
This not only protects the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania, but protects the first responders on our roads around the district. Read the article [here](https://us.list-manage.com/13TK_f5PzPd?e=131e83a3c2&c2id=e7faf2081078228733221dbd5e122ac9).
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/vjV5FIn89eQ?e=131e83a3c2&c2id=e7faf2081078228733221dbd5e122ac9)
|
---
| |
Last week, the Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner visited the district in Hazelton at an Opportunity Center. Rob and Turner focused on revitalizing the area to bring more economic investments to the surrounding community. A rising tide lifts all boats and Rob is laser-focused on creating those opportunities for Northeastern Pennsylvania.

subject: Charlie warned us about this...
body:
This is exactly what he warned about| | | [](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=52fd033efd2c4165a47b59f3ed78d81a&_e=B4PdX2oppA0ohqt1nMPTXR35xr5iU9kOVXzpi65cJy6g4s2LckKFViQ7WpfceaN1NTQp0sHcZTf73JYHabkAqoNF-ZmMGN7x85aI06fC_yInbaYN9uDygXoNRqMs1OclwDAUo30umELJlHi7xQjv5qUT63AaQBgG6wQVYhQKCCM0P90ILISc1pscLzV6px6jjdBdOC3mJAgwBCidr44mE3IOR16L9LqQ6c6caGAEtJ4cUrFu6SvljabLWM0y4JO_ZOEHbXv3xBcfMWjbYD8a4fx4dnMjMaHc2MttYFmiS4w9BOdoqEy3-ANctDpk_bpcc4Y3RHT1kYiJzIqAopeOgJ9vAmxVHTTrxXaT_Cqq4OjusJmwT_2jkqL9kd0RkWFElsFQg8U3115t7FIEPLWDM7jsXA9dgc3vVc5bl2PNInXoag8hG-hsJpeJTzUeKXzZ5ow8TzYh0XlFfRyukN8-FM0XCWAa43JRxrlrRkPjTL5GQdhoLA2f8VCEiJGNxuRKtUj8SGe4JoZ4E9e8UbJem9eqU5P0cHMDF_qQxb1JIRZbZbwY5jRYIBbtpBTBf5UhAgJbk4hyPqjCb-YrCd9KApSc49Bc0q41R5gYxP3nOZk7OSxudHqOKrkehXXykrwW96m4GCVsUXh8lEoe_yPQgaaje2G8OfdIJjO5m7oGg1pxLu3imEGs8kSrVyeI8UEFS9O1rCimg-0iCCLoa2SMsWDireIH6UJfACryt_Yus0M%3D)
---
| | Fellow Patriot,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=52fd033efd2c4165a47b59f3ed78d81a&_e=B4PdX2oppA0ohqt1nMPTXR35xr5iU9kOVXzpi65cJy6g4s2LckKFViQ7WpfceaN1NTQp0sHcZTf73JYHabkAqoNF-ZmMGN7x85aI06fC_yInbaYN9uDygXoNRqMs1OclwDAUo30umELJlHi7xQjv5qUT63AaQBgG6wQVYhQKCCM0P90ILISc1pscLzV6px6jjdBdOC3mJAgwBCidr44mE3IOR16L9LqQ6c6caGAEtJ4cUrFu6SvljabLWM0y4JO_ZOEHbXv3xBcfMWjbYD8a4cw9P9aBZ8lLZvV7DlNv8vdKUGKD_Wonq2aW7E2lHYmUrU4hVjVtGi0kKvA1nDjn_wUn8KT1pxZxukH4EeKJ5TrWE9GhoB9cf3bLXgTb6jlmZuLiSiURHdAC_APztFGkTZtS_aERjzWHTkwmy6ya86taBj07fzxaPGqPKa-DMJ7tao0FJLmCy-9OuLGcxiJNBl9S2Vi1KJCWbt6c6b7hGxnD4E_y4Vc5LBO6OnGmeh1E50_TaA0EEQLYew2uqdyKQOZvAp62jh2zYncY4HomKhEmANBHBnEy0jUywgxmQE7_WrNJbOyBwQ3nS5sv3wW69zt7cvn6gdYU_iKFAaRyheD9NdjEhBzgHwM56MZuhgc76VIhlnSa8g22eOUVkNv6q74WpwsdECyG64Qw0IG3MZg2I7EaHZwoigv5cJ_iMFebASbZM6fYpk65RY5LneDgc4JQTD0i97jEVUkEShCJb0E%3D)
---
We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

**Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. **
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=52fd033efd2c4165a47b59f3ed78d81a&_e=B4PdX2oppA0ohqt1nMPTXR35xr5iU9kOVXzpi65cJy6g4s2LckKFViQ7WpfceaN1NTQp0sHcZTf73JYHabkAqoNF-ZmMGN7x85aI06fC_yInbaYN9uDygXoNRqMs1OclwDAUo30umELJlHi7xQjv5qUT63AaQBgG6wQVYhQKCCM0P90ILISc1pscLzV6px6jjdBdOC3mJAgwBCidr44mE3IOR16L9LqQ6c6caGAEtJ4cUrFu6SvljabLWM0y4JO_ZOEHbXv3xBcfMWjbYD8a4dUxz8szTfibHCRYJpcnqY3N95H76Mi5ZRr2sbuk0KgRrdOV-XqdHvkKJmOuDjnW-AFjS0C7vXR4u9AFxa6A9UHXtHrw5GqL0g4PoXSQbYKhASan5b4Tbe0SftZEcPtVo_0pGef_1kjb1Le4yTSDQ44vdPZGgB-XAAQi_JR621v3qFJ4YYD0GUWBkx1IHHKDshWaHbPFjVwmAHRSQa_J3xEY982Ji6lU-qYXMRlo6bwfWXy12C_wBfsymZSGgoHZ1x7m-rY31xjHdgH439nT-oVwl8t-qp5AfgC4USw_eAKtgqRy-JEWJC_-Fg1CrHvNawfbxw9QSeD--dL3yBlRKW-W7ebSv9DXCWDoHPL05Ax11UNiqBlAK9J7mvX-tbNKKcEq1FNEpQwIZ60aiLlGOKLLSy7QvSva8I2WsvmYBY30OxQ8k-XJxLhp35vvYuWiERb_-IaBCLRsLgg8tJi0ypM%3D)
---
_But now, Fellow Patriot, the question is... _

**What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? **

Because here's the truth:

These students aren't just signing up. _They 're stepping up. _

They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous.

But that isn't stopping them.

They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever.

They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, _but brave_. Not just loud, but _principled_.

**Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. **

**We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. **

These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses.

Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship.

**[If you’re able to, I hope you’ll help send a kit to the next student who raises their hand to lead by making your gift to Turning Point USA today.](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=52fd033efd2c4165a47b59f3ed78d81a&_e=B4PdX2oppA0ohqt1nMPTXR35xr5iU9kOVXzpi65cJy6g4s2LckKFViQ7WpfceaN1NTQp0sHcZTf73JYHabkAqoNF-ZmMGN7x85aI06fC_yInbaYN9uDygXoNRqMs1OclwDAUo30umELJlHi7xQjv5qUT63AaQBgG6wQVYhQKCCM0P90ILISc1pscLzV6px6jjdBdOC3mJAgwBCidr44mE3IOR16L9LqQ6c6caGAEtJ4cUrFu6SvljabLWM0y4JO_ZOEHbXv3xBcfMWjbYD8a4YKsGzwoniHeLAuoFJeWkCyNCbOQpDqfsFbZaamClxugUHVzTUkw4z6F2hyUjs9RHv6A58s-DLbXL-3uR0kcoh3WD2vj0sque2d0uTuwjALP9cSkMwsqKi3gvC8BNQhK5JdcQaKPeFYBKqSztN0oT3DgEL0A-cZRPo-E1OyNunsrPoPLBWlnNGmm8vFROZyojVYWjGqE7xvgOg9vT32Yu9HoFMECGUWLrhb4r0PwZJdayqyZQ9IjB5PZE1Rf4pKcPJHKv8jE6NyDECILhaZuLbJL7SOHDEKZUT1uVMlgrc6gJ4_04rhv2l7igzD2hvYWZuhwL4YVf-q4_Hg5x8YGwnhcB7Vh_ghet2JKd6cEVtF3FMfFoBFs7w4810qBXJvkiacreGe5jlqjyH7ocXDikXeJBm6Gg-nJ7ixr7Awq41xwQtB6j8I1C9rQgPWZHKMy_mUPQOhVlEealB2t40_4_kc%3D)**

name: Patty Murray
subject: The GOP's big, ugly betrayal of Americans, one year later
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY PEOPLE FOR PATTY MURRAY
body:
It's working exactly as Republicans planned.
| | |
---
The big, ugly betrayal of a bill is working exactly as Republicans planned:
* _At least 4 million people – including 800,000 kids – lost food assistance._
* _Nearly 5 million were kicked off Medicaid and CHIP combined. _
* _ACA premiums shot up 58% across the board – some skyrocketing 10X._
* _More than 1.2 million people were forced to drop health coverage entirely._
* _Household energy bills are up $110._

Behind all of those numbers are real people, Peter – family, neighbors, co-workers, classmates. Fellow Americans, like you and me.
**All of us are worse off now than a year ago, when Republicans passed Donald Trump's crowning achievement: the largest transfer of wealth from the poor to the rich in U.S. history.**
Republicans are turning a blind eye to the damage their bill has caused, not because they’re surprised by the outcome, but because it’s working exactly as they planned: Sell out working families to make sure Donald Trump and his billionaire and trillionaire allies benefit.
But I refuse to let the GOP get away with this – and I've spent the last 365+ days working relentlessly to turn the tide. **_[The best thing we can do to stop the full extent of harm in store for folks nationwide is to build up the grassroots war chest to show the GOP we're fired up to fire them.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135212863/633476999/-11758678?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk669-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjdiZDQyYy0wZDdmLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=CpB8JZYxptzNiVxkvXie87RCXf9HRRXQ6RdXFpCnHqA=)_**
Look – when my dad got MS and couldn't keep working, we didn't have an income for the few months it took my mom to learn new skills and get a bookkeeping job. Food stamps helped put food on the table for my six siblings and me over that time.
**Back then, we lived in a country where the government didn’t just say, “You’re on your own.” **

Everyone tells you the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is beyond hope. Dr. [Debra Shushan](https://open.substack.com/users/315292076-debra-shushan?utm_source=mentions) doesn't buy it. In this conversation, she and [Lawrence Winnerman](https://open.substack.com/users/314034871-lawrence-winnerman?utm_source=mentions) walk through **A Land for All** --the confederation plan built by Israelis and Palestinians together that rethinks what a border even is: two sovereign states, open borders, a shared Jerusalem, and a workable answer on refugees.

subject: The summer gap
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
We’ve got to beat the summer slowdown.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260713-1&t=1&akid=3717%2E587540%2EtpAM1h)
Peter, I know it's summer.
You’re probably busy, trying to catch up on some rest, or maybe even away on vacation. Honestly, I don't blame you. We all need a break.
But because everyone is rightfully unplugging, political giving drops off a cliff during these months. It’s what we call the "summer fundraising slump" — and right now, it’s hitting us exactly when we can’t afford a gap.
Our young, progressive candidates are out on the pavement right now — in the brutal summer heat — knocking doors, building campaigns from scratch, and fighting to break the right-wing supermajorities crushing our future.
They are doing the grueling, necessary work to change this country. But they cannot do it if our funding stalls out. We back our candidates by sending mail pieces to voters in their districts, creating ads to amplify their message, conducting polls so they know precisely where to allocate their resources, and much more. Our support can tip the scales in a race, so now is not the time to let up.
And I’ll let you in on a secret: The wealthy, ultra-dense networks of dark money donors we’re up against don't stop writing checks to our opponents just because it’s July. That means it’s more important than ever that we don’t slow down.
The most impactful thing you can do to support us today is to start a recurring contribution to Leaders We Deserve. That’s why I’m asking, Peter:
**[Will you become a Summer Sustainer and donate $5 monthly to power our mission electing young progressives through Election Day and beyond?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260713_1_summersr.ESPCI2&refcode=em20260713-3717&amount=5&t=2&akid=3717%2E587540%2EtpAM1h)**

David Hogg

subject: BREAKING: Justices Barrett and Kagan to testify in the Senate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Democracy
body:
When the Supreme Court justices arrive at the Capitol tomorrow, what will they hear? | |
---
Peter, Tomorrow, Supreme Court Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan are testifying before Congress to request more taxpayer dollars. **It will be the first time the justices have testified in committee in 15 years—and it comes just weeks after the Supreme Court ended a term in which they rewrote the rules of the game.** **We cannot allow Congress to treat this like business as usual.** We deserve answers. We deserve for our demands to be heard. We deserve a democracy that’s built for us, not the wannabe dictator and the wealthy extremists pulling his strings. [**This is a rare opportunity, when Justices will appear before Congress under oath. We need to make sure Congress takes advantage and demands accountability! Can you send a message to your Senators urging them to hold the Court accountable?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxCdZvuHTfb3SsWLrrEMExlxWnBQ7yGUd3QY3YDypVNStpRKm-8TKKwUL_qh-UHwClsORmcl3OJnanPtwOd6n39P-ZwF2CAZsB6j3ZKyCiPWeY_iBT5bd7N-bbLajowk4T8meTQFXqL78niXE-425DsRLI6DGyFnK_6yhYjiuO3zaYvzfml36ZOBM3Nq6xfQVTMTAbz0-8ExhzZ_Om3x47198RJ4o3WhcIc9l58lUtSa6L9N3IBWHdDvVCTI0c9LZ5PzQ9CVsoDvPD_PsrAjSAdImcGMohyieQhzRXgrYaIds30zbobmNKUVegm0OmMBLBPycJ1aMG_y-pvfvrM698Pmel3bAFmTQG-fDVnA-95zY/4sa/Sz9v8G8nQm6fNG2S4FxaLw/h0/h001.bx19cDic1zw0bpjQYvZ7_fkgna8iAMlpCiHQfOeGcDY) Everyday, working families across the country are struggling to afford gas, groceries, rent, healthcare, and childcare. They’re facing ICE terror in the streets. They’re watching our power be ripped from us and handed directly to the billionaires and corporations making our lives harder. **The Wall Street-controlled justices on the Supreme Court have only made things worse. They’ve ruled in Trump’s favor 90% of the time. They made it possible for wealthy extremists to rig the system. And now they’ve gutted fair representation and cemented corporate power for decades to come.** Worse still, they believe that nothing can hold them accountable. clean_body: When the Supreme Court justices arrive at the Capitol tomorrow, what will they hear? | | Peter, Tomorrow, Supreme Court Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan are testifying before Congress to request more taxpayer dollars. It will be the first time the justices have testified in committee in 15 years—and it comes just weeks after the Supreme Court ended a term in which they rewrote the rules of the game. We cannot allow Congress to treat this like business as usual. We deserve answers. We deserve for our demands to be heard. We deserve a democracy that’s built for us, not the wannabe dictator and the wealthy extremists pulling his strings. Everyday, working families across the country are struggling to afford gas, groceries, rent, healthcare, and childcare. They’re facing ICE terror in the streets. They’re watching our power be ripped from us and handed directly to the billionaires and corporations making our lives harder. The Wall Street-controlled justices on the Supreme Court have only made things worse. They’ve ruled in Trump’s favor 90% of the time. They made it possible for wealthy extremists to rig the system. And now they’ve gutted fair representation and cemented corporate power for decades to come. Worse still, they believe that nothing can hold them accountable. It’s up to We the People to demand accountability, an end to corruption and unchecked power, and a system that actually works for our communities. They work for us! As an immigrant growing up in poverty, Rima found stability and opportunity in public schools.
Her family came here when she was 5 years old, and their experience with displacement and rebuilding their lives in multiple countries shaped how she approaches immigration policy — with urgency, compassion, and a focus on dignity.
**While serving as a school board trustee, Rima has pushed to protect the privacy and safety of immigrant students and families** , including safeguarding immigration status information and ensuring training for teachers and staff.
She has supported **school policies that protect LGBTQ+ students** and ensure inclusivity and safety. She also supported **transitioning from diesel to electric school buses and installing solar panels on school rooftops** — prioritizing underserved communities, where environmental and health burdens are often greatest and infrastructure investment has historically lagged.
In college, Will built a **national student network of students working for fossil fuel divestment**. And while serving as a community organizer, he has fought for good jobs and housing, **organized food drives** for thousands of families, and **canceled $100,000 in medical debt** for his neighbors.
Will is demanding lower costs of living, Medicare for All, a federal moratorium on data centers, an arms embargo to stop weapons sales to Israel and other human rights violators, and a ban on stock trading by federal lawmakers.
He’s running against two corporate Democrats in Michigan’s August 4th congressional primary election, to ultimately defeat the district’s corporate-backed Republican representative this fall.
A majority of my colleagues are millionaires who take money from corporate PACs and AIPAC. I need people like Will Lawrence by my side in Congress.
