clean_body: Rima and Will are people-powered candidates who are deeply rooted in their communities. | | | Friend, I’m excited to endorse two candidates who are movement leaders and community organizers: Rima Mohammad and Will Lawrence. Will co-founded the environmental justice organization Sunrise Movement, where he helped draft the Green New Deal. He also founded the Michigan Rent Is Too Damn High Coalition, which has won statewide protections for low-income renters, and the Mid-Michigan Tenant Resource Center, which has helped families avoid homelessness. He’s now running for U.S. Congress in Michigan’s 7th district, a swing district that’s currently represented by a Big-Oil-backed Republican. We need Will to win so we can flip the U.S. House of Representatives, stop Trump’s and Republicans’ agenda, take on the billionaires and warmongers and corporate polluters who profit off our pain, and join me in the fight for Medicare for All and a federal moratorium on AI data centers. Rima Mohammad co-founded the People’s Coalition, a Michigan organization and PAC dedicated to equity and progressive change. A Palestinian refugee whose life was transformed by her public school experience, Rima was the first Arab American elected to the Ann Arbor Public Schools Board. Now she’s running for re-election to continue supporting marginalized students. Rima and Will are both unbought and people-powered, running grassroots campaigns that are deeply rooted in their communities. | As an immigrant growing up in poverty, Rima found stability and opportunity in public schools. Her family came here when she was 5 years old, and their experience with displacement and rebuilding their lives in multiple countries shaped how she approaches immigration policy — with urgency, compassion, and a focus on dignity. While serving as a school board trustee, Rima has pushed to protect the privacy and safety of immigrant students and families , including safeguarding immigration status information and ensuring training for teachers and staff. She has supported school policies that protect LGBTQ+ students and ensure inclusivity and safety. She also supported transitioning from diesel to electric school buses and installing solar panels on school rooftops — prioritizing underserved communities, where environmental and health burdens are often greatest and infrastructure investment has historically lagged. In college, Will built a national student network of students working for fossil fuel divestment. And while serving as a community organizer, he has fought for good jobs and housing, organized food drives for thousands of families, and canceled $100,000 in medical debt for his neighbors. Will is demanding lower costs of living, Medicare for All, a federal moratorium on data centers, an arms embargo to stop weapons sales to Israel and other human rights violators, and a ban on stock trading by federal lawmakers. He’s running against two corporate Democrats in Michigan’s August 4th congressional primary election, to ultimately defeat the district’s corporate-backed Republican representative this fall. A majority of my colleagues are millionaires who take money from corporate PACs and AIPAC. I need people like Will Lawrence by my side in Congress. subject: Running, rock music, and green chile salsa
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/13477?refcode=em-header%3Frefcode%3Djtk990-fr-nd&t=1&akid=10927%2E400544%2EXQsaMp)
---
Friend,
You want to know what energizes me every day? Early morning runs in beautiful New Mexico, loud rock music, and cooking my green chile salsa.
I love starting my day before sunrise with a cup of coffee. Getting outside for a run or a walk reconnects me with the same land my Pueblo ancestors stewarded for generations and reminds me why this work matters.
Then I'll usually catch up on the news, grab a breakfast burrito, and hit the road.
These days, I spend most of my time traveling from town to town, meeting New Mexicans, listening to their stories, and hearing what's on their minds.
And what I'm hearing is clear: New Mexicans need a fighter. Families are worried about the cost of groceries, gas, housing, and healthcare. I've lived those struggles firsthand. I raised my child as a single mom, and I know exactly what grocery store math feels like. That's why I'm running — to lower costs, protect our land and water, strengthen our schools, and make sure every New Mexican has a fair shot.
The stakes in this Governor's race couldn't be higher. We're up against a Republican opponent who wants to take us backward, and MAGA donors are pouring hundreds of thousands of dollars into his campaign to make that a reality.
**That’s why I’m personally asking:_[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can spare before tonight's deadline so we can win this race and deliver progress for New Mexico's working families?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/13160?refcode=jtk990-fr-nd&t=2&akid=10927%2E400544%2EXQsaMp)_**

Thanks for being by my side, day after day.

– Deb

name: Lizzie Fletcher
subject: All that is going on in Houston today
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Today is a day I love to celebrate every year—it’s 713 Day in Houston, recognizing our city’s original area code and celebrating the people and places that make our city great.
This year, however, it comes on a day when our community is grieving the death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo after ICE agents shot him on the streets of Houston last week. And the lighthearted fun we have on 713 Day feels a little different when our hearts are so heavy.
Last week, I joined members of Houston’s congressional delegation in demanding answers and an independent investigation; I visited the site where he was killed; and I gathered with labor leaders, elected officials, and people from across our community for a vigil to honor and remember Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, to pledge our support for his family and our community, and to share our commitment to seeking truth and justice.
As I shared with those gathered at the vigil this weekend, my heart has been heavy for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo's family, which has lost a father, a husband, a brother, and more; for our community, which has lost a neighbor and a friend; and for our country, which feels like it has lost its way.
It was just last weekend that we celebrated Independence Day—a day where our founders declared that all men are created equal, and have unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. And this week, agents of the federal government took the life of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo on the streets of Houston, denying him all three.
Sadly, we learned today that ICE has shot and killed another person in Maine.
When I was in school, history was my favorite class. So I know that in our history in this country, we have not always lived up to our highest ideals or the promises made in our Declaration of Independence or in our Constitution. But I also know that we have not abandoned those ideals or the promise of liberty and justice for all.
And we must not abandon them now. Now more than ever, we must work together to protect the people of America and to protect the promise of America.
And that is why heading to the Open House at our campaign office later that day was the best thing I could have done following the heartbreaking vigil. That room was full of people who continue to show up again and again to do what we need to do right now: protect the people and the promise of America. We’ve been doing it on our campaign since 2017, and we are not stopping now.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe260713?refcode=lpfe260713 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe260713?refcode=lpfe260713]
We've got real work ahead this year—and in the years ahead. This year’s mid-term elections are critical to moving our country in a better direction. As are the 2028 elections. More rulings from the Supreme Court and announcements from the White House last week make it clear that we must fight everywhere to ensure people can cast their ballots safely. Whether it's the disbanding of the independent election commission that helps state and local governments, the enabling of even more big money in our elections, and the insistence on passing the incredibly dangerous SAVE Act, Republicans are focused on making it harder to vote, denying people a voice in our government.
And that brings us back to what gives me hope today: the people in the 713 who have been doing and will continue to do the work to participate in democracy, to protect it, and to empower the people who live here and across the country to fulfill the promises and make real the possibility of America. We’ve been doing it here on this team for nearly a decade, and we are not stopping now.
Together, we can do anything.

| Hamilton Headlines Good afternoon! The General Assembly completed work on Virginia’s new two-year state budget on June 29, just before it took effect on July 1, 2026. The final package totals approximately $205 billion, including federal, general-fund and other state revenues. It also incorporated the 14 final amendments from Governor Spanberger. Here are the primary provisions affecting local communities: ~$2 billion new public education funding4% raises for teachers/school support staff (split between state/local)3.5% raises for state employees$577 million for childcare and early-childhood education$349.7 million for higher education School Resource Officers:Funding was cut by nearly 25%. from approximately $20.4 million to $15.9 million, a reduction of about $4.5 million per year. The budget also transfers $10 million in unused SRO fund balances to the General Fund. SRO's are vital to securing school campuses and I was deeply troubled to see this program cut. Local Law Enforcement:The budget provides no increase in HB 599 funding, the state assistance program for local police departments. It also eliminates a proposed $2 million reimbursement program for local law-enforcement agencies transporting individuals under emergency custody or temporary detention orders. RGGI and Energy Costs:Democrats chose to increase all of our power bills by reentering Virginia into the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative on July 1. Power companies will purchase carbon allowances and the estimated $500 million/yr expense is expected to be passed on to customers. Under the final budget, 45% of RGGI revenue must be returned as bill credits to eligible residential, small-business and church customers. This is the state taking a dollar from you, giving you back 45 cents, and trying to rebrand it as "affordability". The Governor’s amendment expressly includes customers of rural electric cooperatives. Unfortunately, municipality owned electric companies did not get included in the rebate, leaving out many customers across the commonwealth. New Taxes and Programs:The budget creates a first-in-the-nation electricity-consumption tax on data centers, projected to generate approximately $600 million annually. This consumption tax will expire in two years, while the controversial data center sales tax break will remain in place until 2035. Governor Spanberger also signed a bill into law that implements mandatory 12 week paid family and medical leave in Virginia for the first time. This bill imposes new payroll taxes, split by Virginia businesses and employees, beginning on April 1, 2028. The budget allows for localities to hold a referendum to increase our Virginia sales tax by 1% with the proceeds funding local government. While many localities will be eager to implement this, these taxes primarily benefit areas with significant shopping centers and retail, rather than the rural areas that need the revenue. For instance, of the 4 counties I represent, none of them have an indoor shopping mall or bulk shopping store, and only two have a Walmart. That means rural residents from Orange and Madison counties will be primarily paying into the areas they shop in (likely Culpeper, Greene or Fredericksburg) rather than their home counties. Their tax dollars will be funneled away from where they reside, into more developed counties to benefit their schools and county services. While this choice will ultimtately be put to voters on the ballot, this is something to keep in mind. New or expanded programs: -$150 million for state health-insurance premium assistance-$350 million Medicaid reserve-$225 million federal-contingency-$60 million for housing initiatives-$25 million for energy-efficiency and weatherization programs (green energy subsidies)-$16 million for the Safer Communities Program Additional amendments establish a professional firefighter cancer-screening grant program funded at approximately $2 million annually, accelerate pay increases for home-care workers and to establish a new Virginia Digital Service team. In conclusion, this budget makes major new investments in education, healthcare, housing and state programs. It expands government and spends an additional 9 million more dollars per day. Local governments face challenges ahead due to reduced SRO funding, stagnant HB 599 law-enforcement assistance, and teacher pay increases being higher than locally budgeted. These unfunded mandates and unexpected cuts strain localities, potentially leading to a difficult decision--cut services, burden local taxpayers, or seek out new sources of revenue to cover the gap.

# We're Building a Better Democratic Party by Telling You the Truth
### We need your help to keep doing it
| | | [Laura Rodriguez-Carbone](https://substack.com/@whispercampaign)
---
| Jul 13
---
| [](https://substack.com/@whispercampaign)
---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60b09823-db9c-4f8e-80db-edddddd1ac53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You've probably gotten a thousand fundraising emails over the years that made your skin crawl. Panic in the subject line, a fake deadline for FEC reports, guilt trips, and never a word about where the money you donated actually went.
This is not one of those e-mails.
Matt and I are going to tell you exactly what we're building and exactly what your donation pays for..
If you already know this work is worth funding, you can do it right now.
**-> [Give once here](https://substack.com/redirect/9835c0b2-6658-46be-9387-ba34d51a1e90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
We're two Democrats who want the party to do better and be better. The Angry Democrats, the Angry Ohioans, and the Whisper Campaign are running independent political coverage that explains the news and the strategy underneath what the party is doing and how it does it both locally and in DC to make sure you have the full understanding of the politics that affect your family, your friends, and your wallet. We hold our own party to the same standards as we would any Republican, by name, which is the whole reason our coverage will never get an insider's check.
So here is the ask. [A one-time gift toward the next issue.](https://substack.com/redirect/9835c0b2-6658-46be-9387-ba34d51a1e90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This coverage runs on readers, not on party committees or party donors. If you already subscribe, thank you, and a one-time gift goes beyond what the subscription can stretch to cover. If you have been reading and have not subscribed yet, a gift is a way to put real weight behind the work today.
`$25` covers the hours to break down a race the day it breaks. `$50 `covers the research behind a full strategy piece. `$100` helps publish the analysis the insiders would rather you never read. Give what its worth to you.
**-> [Fund the next piece](https://substack.com/redirect/9835c0b2-6658-46be-9387-ba34d51a1e90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Every dollar funds coverage you can read and the worked needed to curate the stories, strategy, and analysis to bring you the information you need to know.
[Give once](https://substack.com/redirect/9835c0b2-6658-46be-9387-ba34d51a1e90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Then hold us to it.
### Stay Angry.
Laura & Matt

Berea, Ohio
